through both modes, in parallel, with seeded fixtures. Its test is the
reference for how to write yours.


# Source: observability.md

# Observability hooks

Momo calls the hooks you register with `momo.WithHook` around every statement
(`momo.Hook`) and around every relation load (`momo.RelationHook`, for a hook
that also implements it). The interfaces live in the root package because `DB`
calls them. Ready-made implementations:

| Hook           | Constructor                                  | What it does                                                                                      |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `obs.Recorder` | `&obs.Recorder{}` (package `obs`)            | Keeps every finished statement and relation load for assertions in tests.                         |
| `obs.NPlusOne` | `obs.NewNPlusOne(n, report)` (`obs`)         | Reports a relation that was loaded more than `n` times inside one `obs.WithScope`.                |
| slow query     | `obs.NewSlowQuery(d, report, opts...)`       | Reports each statement slower than `d`, with an opt-in plain `EXPLAIN` plan.                      |
| slog hook      | `momolog.New(logger, opts...)` (`momolog`)   | Logs one `log/slog` record per statement and one per relation load (see [slog](#slog)).           |
| OTel hook      | `otelmomo.New(tp, mp, opts...)` (`otelmomo`) | Emits a client span and a duration histogram per statement (see [OpenTelemetry](#opentelemetry)). |

`obs` imports only `momo` and the standard library. All of these hooks are safe
for concurrent use.

## Arguments and sensitive columns

A hook sees bound argument values only when the DB was opened with
`momo.WithArgLogging`. A value bound from a column tagged `sensitive` reaches
every hook as `momo.RedactedArg` (`[redacted]`), never as the real value, and
the hooks here cannot recover it. `obs.Recorder` stores a copy of the arguments and
hands out copies. The slog hook logs arguments only when you also pass
`momolog.Values(true)`.

## Recorder

```text
rec := &obs.Recorder{}
db := momo.New(drv, momo.WithHook(rec))
// run the code under test
rec.SQLs()      // the SQL text of each statement, in order
rec.Events()    // the full momo.QueryEvent of each, plus CtxSQL
rec.Relations() // the momo.RelationEvent of each relation load, with its Err
rec.Reset()
```

`obs.Event.CtxSQL` is the value `obs.Recorder` put into the context in `BeforeQuery`; it
equals `SQL` when the context reached `AfterQuery` intact, which makes it a
check that the hook chain passes the context through.

## N+1 detection

Two detectors exist, and they count different things:

| Detector               | Counts                                        | Scope                      | Use it for                                           |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `obs.NewNPlusOne`      | relation loads (`Load`, `LoadAll`, `Preload`) | `obs.WithScope(ctx)`       | a relation `Load` inside a loop over the parents     |
| `momo.NewNPlusOneHook` | repeated statement shapes                     | `momo.WithQueryScope(ctx)` | any repeated statement, such as a `Select` in a loop |

Use either or both. Each reads only its own scope, so a context needs
`obs.WithScope` for the first and `momo.WithQueryScope` for the second; a
context with only one of them is not tracked by the other detector.

```text
det := obs.NewNPlusOne(3, func(f obs.Finding) {
    log.Printf("N+1: %s loaded %d times", f.Relation, f.Count)
})
db := momo.New(drv, momo.WithHook(det))

ctx := obs.WithScope(r.Context()) // one request, one job
```

`obs.NPlusOne` counts relation loads per relation within a scope. It reports
once per relation and scope, when the count first exceeds the threshold. One
batched `Load` is one load however many parents it covers, so it never triggers
a finding; a `Load` inside a loop over the parents does. `obs.Finding.Parents` is
the parent count of the load that crossed the threshold; 1 is the usual sign of
a loop. A context without a scope is not tracked, a scope tracks at most 1024
relations, and a panic in `report` is recovered and dropped. `report` runs on
the loading goroutine and must not query the database. Create the detector with
`obs.NewNPlusOne`; its zero value must not be used.

## Slow queries

`obs.NewSlowQuery(threshold, report)` calls `report` with an `obs.SlowQuery`
(`SQL`, `Duration`, and `Plan` or `PlanSkipped`) for each statement that took
longer than `threshold`.

```text
plain := momo.New(drv) // a DB without the slow-query hook
db := momo.New(drv, momo.WithHook(obs.NewSlowQuery(200*time.Millisecond,
    func(q obs.SlowQuery) { log.Printf("slow %s: %s %v", q.Duration, q.SQL, q.Plan) },
    obs.WithPlainExplain(plain),
)))
```

Without `obs.WithPlainExplain` the report has no plan. With it, the hook runs
one plain `EXPLAIN` for the slow statement, never `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, so nothing
runs twice. Outside a transaction the plan comes from the querier you pass;
inside a transaction it runs on that transaction in a savepoint that is always
rolled back, so a plan that fails cannot abort your transaction. Cases where
there is no plan say why in `PlanSkipped`: a statement with bound arguments on a
DB opened without `momo.WithArgLogging`, a statement that binds a sensitive
value, a transaction that is already aborted (PostgreSQL), and an `EXPLAIN` the
database rejected. The statements the hook issues for the plan are not reported
again. `report` runs on the goroutine that ran the statement and must not query
the database. The plan can echo literal values.

## Explain

`momo.Explain(ctx, q, compiled)` returns the database's plan for any compiled
statement (the value of a query's `SQL` method) without running it: `EXPLAIN` on
PostgreSQL, `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on SQLite and `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON` on MySQL
and MariaDB. `momo.ExplainAnalyze(ctx, q, compiled)` runs the statement under
`EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, FORMAT TEXT)` and returns the plan with actual timings. It
executes the statement, so every call, a `SELECT` included, runs inside a
transaction (a savepoint on a `Tx`) that is always rolled back. A rollback
cannot undo what happens outside the transaction: sequence values taken by
`nextval`, `NOTIFY` sent by a function, work done through `dblink` or a foreign
data wrapper. A `SELECT` that calls such a function still has those effects. It
is PostgreSQL only: other dialects return `ErrUnsupported` and send nothing. Momo calls
neither on its own, and hooks see both as Op `explain`.
`SelectQuery.Explain` stays the shorthand for a select.

## slog

The slog hook is `momolog.New`; there is one slog hook, not two.

```text
logger := slog.New(slog.NewJSONHandler(os.Stderr, nil))
db := momo.New(drv, momo.WithHook(momolog.New(logger,
    momolog.Level(slog.LevelInfo),
    momolog.SlowOver(200*time.Millisecond), // slower statements log at WARN
)))
```

A statement record (`momo.query`) has `op`, `table`, `relation` (when set),
`sql`, `duration`, `rows`, `err` (when set) and, with `momolog.Values(true)` and
`momo.WithArgLogging`, `args`. A relation record (`momo.relation`) has `parent`,
`name`, `kind`, `parents`, `children`, `queries`, `duration` and `err` (when
set). Errors are logged through `Error()` only.

## OpenTelemetry

`otelmomo` is a separate module, `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/otelmomo`, so the
Momo core links no OpenTelemetry package (a test runs `go list -deps` on the core
to keep it that way). Add it to your `go.mod` only if you want it.

The module has its own release tags, `otelmomo/vX.Y.Z`, made by release-please
(`go get github.com/azrtydxb/momo/otelmomo@latest`). It requires a released momo
version (see its `go.mod`) whose exported API it compiles against, so it needs
no unreleased momo code;
the `replace` directive in its `go.mod` only points in-repository builds at the
working tree and is ignored by anyone who imports it. A repository test fails if
that require ever becomes a pseudo-version or names a momo version newer than
the last release.

```text
h, err := otelmomo.New(tracerProvider, meterProvider, otelmomo.WithNamespace("appdb"))
if err != nil {
    return err // a nil provider is an error; there is no global fallback
}
db := momo.New(drv, momo.WithHook(h))
```

The providers are passed in; the package reads no global provider. Each
statement becomes a client span named `<OPERATION> <table>` (`SELECT authors`),
or `<OPERATION>` when no table is known, with the database client attributes
`db.system.name` (`postgresql`, `sqlite`, `mysql`, `mariadb`),
`db.operation.name`, `db.collection.name`, `db.namespace` (from `WithNamespace`)
and `db.query.text`. The query text is the parameterized SQL; the value of a
bound argument is never recorded, not even with `momo.WithArgLogging`. A failed
statement sets the span status to error and `error.type`. The same hook records
the `db.client.operation.duration` histogram (unit `s`) with the same
attributes plus `error.type` on failure.

## Tenants

Tenant isolation stays row-level security through `WithTxSetup`; `obs` adds no
tenant helper.


# Source: PRIVACY_RULES.md

# Interceptors: application-level statement rules

An interceptor is a function attached to one `*momo.DB` handle with `momo.WithInterceptor`. It runs before the typed statements of that handle, may append predicates to them, and may deny them by returning an error. **It is an application-level guard, not a privacy or security boundary: it filters only the primary table of the typed Select, Insert, Upsert, Update, SoftDelete and Delete builders, and every path listed under "What an interceptor does not cover" bypasses it.** Use it to remove accidents, and use database row-level security where isolation must hold when application code is wrong.

## What an interceptor sees

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
type Operation struct {
    Kind  string      // "select", "insert", "upsert", "update", "delete", "truncate"
    Table string
    Where []Predicate // starts empty; append to it
}

type Interceptor func(ctx context.Context, op *Operation) error
```

- Select, update and delete: the predicates in `Where` are ANDed to the statement and appear in the SQL that `SQL` returns and that the hooks see.
- Insert and upsert: the interceptor runs so it can deny the statement; predicates appended to them are ignored. It runs when the statement executes (`Exec`, `Rows`), never for `SQL`, which for an insert runs neither interceptors nor hooks.
- An `Upsert`, or an `Insert` with `OnConflict` and `DoUpdate`, has the kind `upsert`, not `insert`. ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE can overwrite an existing row, including a row of another tenant that shares the conflict key, and an appended predicate cannot stop it. A tenant rule must therefore deny the kind `upsert` or constrain it by other means (see the recipe). An `Insert` with `DoNothing` is an `insert`.
- A soft delete has the kind `delete`.
- `Truncate` has the kind `truncate`. It removes every row of the table, so a tenant-scoped handle should deny it; a predicate appended to it is ignored.
- `BulkUpdate` is an `update` and keeps the predicates. `Merge` is an `upsert` when it has a matched update and an `insert` otherwise; a predicate an interceptor appends makes it fail with `ErrValidation`, because it cannot be applied without changing which rows match. `InsertQuery.Copy` is an `insert` (deny only).
- Interceptors run in registration order, before the typed model hooks (`Meta.Hooks`), so a denied statement never reaches a Before hook. The first error stops the chain and the statement; it is returned as a `momo.Error` of kind `ErrValidation` that still reaches the interceptor's own error with `errors.Is`. No SQL runs.
- The predicates an interceptor adds are not a caller filter: an update or delete with no `Where` of its own is still refused with `ErrUnfilteredMutation` unless `AllRows` confirms it. A version-checked model update whose row is hidden by an interceptor predicate returns `ErrNotFound`, not `ErrOptimisticLock`. The count that decides between the two is a select, so your select interceptors run for it too.

## The context

Interceptors receive the statement's context, so a tenant usually comes from `ctx`. `SQL`, which has no context argument, runs the interceptors with `context.Background`. An interceptor that reads the tenant from `ctx` sees none there: the SQL it returns shows no tenant predicate, and an interceptor that denies when the tenant is missing denies every `SQL` call. Inspect the statement a handle really runs through the hook events, or give the handle its tenant at construction (below) so the predicate does not depend on `ctx`.

## Recipe: a tenant handle

Build one handle per tenant (or per request) and give it the tenant predicate. The tenant comes from the handle's own configuration, so a statement cannot choose another one.

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
func tenantDB(drv momo.Driver, tenantID int64) *momo.DB {
    return momo.New(drv, momo.WithInterceptor(func(ctx context.Context, op *momo.Operation) error {
        if op.Table != "documents" {
            return nil
        }
        switch op.Kind {
        case "select", "update", "delete":
            op.Where = append(op.Where, DocTenantID.Eq(tenantID))
        case "upsert":
            return errors.New("upsert is not allowed on a tenant handle")
        case "truncate":
            return errors.New("truncate is not allowed on a tenant handle")
        }
        return nil
    }))
}
```

Inserts are not filtered by a predicate: the tenant column of a new row is the model's own value, so set it in a `BeforeInsert` model method (`func (m *Model) BeforeInsert(ctx context.Context) error`, wired into `Meta.Hooks` by `momo generate`) and do not trust the caller to set it. `BeforeInsert` runs only for `Model` and `Models` inserts: `InsertQuery.Values`, `ValuesRows` and `FromSelect` inserts have no model and skip it, so a tenant handle that relies on the hook must also deny those forms, or deny inserts altogether and write through a trusted handle.

A read-only handle denies every write:

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/azrtydxb/momo"
)

func readOnly(drv momo.Driver) *momo.DB {
	return momo.New(drv, momo.WithInterceptor(func(ctx context.Context, op *momo.Operation) error {
		if op.Kind != "select" {
			return fmt.Errorf("handle is read-only: %s on %s", op.Kind, op.Table)
		}
		return nil
	}))
}

func main() { _ = readOnly }
```

## Scope

An interceptor belongs to the handle it was registered on:

- A transaction begun with `Begin` or `Tx` from that handle runs the same interceptors.
- A handle created by another call to `momo.New`, even over the same driver, has none of them.
- Registering an interceptor on one handle never changes another.

## What an interceptor does not cover

Each of these bypasses every interceptor. Scope them explicitly or use row-level security.

- Relation loading: `Load`, `Preload` and `LoadCounts` query the related tables without interceptors.
- Joined relation tables: for a `Joined` relation only the primary table is filtered; the joined table is not.
- The association helpers (`Link`, `Unlink`, `Replace` and the like) and graph creation.
- Subqueries and other sources rendered inside a statement: subquery operands, `UPDATE ... FROM` sources, and the `FromSelect` source of an insert.
- Raw SQL of every kind: `momo.Exec`, `momo.MapRows`, `momo.Scalars`, `momo.Query`, `momo.QueryRows`, `momo.SQL` fragments and `momo.RawSubquery`.
- Bulk loading with COPY: `InsertQuery[T].Copy` runs the insert interceptors (deny only) and `BeforeInsert`, but a predicate an interceptor adds is ignored, and `momo.CopierOf(...).CopyFrom` skips them entirely.
- Anything run on the driver directly, and any other `*momo.DB` over the same driver.

For isolation that holds even when application code is wrong, use database row-level security with the transaction setup hook (`WithTxSetup`) and a policy on the table. Treat interceptors as the first layer and row-level security as the enforcing one.

## Related

- Sensitive columns are masked in hook events: bound values of columns tagged sensitive reach hooks as `momo.RedactedArg`.
- Typed model hooks (`Meta.Hooks`) change values on a model before a write and after a read; `momo generate` fills them from model methods named `BeforeInsert`, `BeforeUpdate`, `BeforeDelete` and `AfterLoad` with the signature `func(context.Context) error`, so there is nothing to set by hand; see the `HookSet` documentation for the semantics and for what a Before hook may leave behind when a statement then fails.


# Source: momovet.md

# momovet: static check for raw SQL

Momo binds every value as a parameter, but the raw-SQL functions take the statement text as a Go string. A string built with `+` or a format call from user input is an injection point. The `momovet` analyzer reports it.

## What it reports

A call to one of these functions of `github.com/azrtydxb/momo` whose SQL argument is not a constant:

| Function           | SQL argument                              |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `momo.Exec`        | third (after the context and the querier) |
| `momo.Scalars`     | third (after the context and the querier) |
| `momo.MapRows`     | third (after the context and the querier) |
| `momo.Query`       | third (after the context and the querier) |
| `momo.QueryRows`   | third (after the context and the querier) |
| `momo.RawQuery`    | second (after the querier)                |
| `momo.SQL`         | first                                     |
| `momo.TypedSQL`    | first                                     |
| `momo.RawSubquery` | first                                     |

A constant is a string literal, a `const`, or an expression made only of constants (`"UPDATE t SET " + "x = 1"`). Anything else is reported as `non-constant SQL string passed to momo.<Name>`. Pass values as arguments after the SQL text instead of concatenating them.

## Running it

```sh
go install github.com/azrtydxb/momo/cmd/momovet@latest
go vet -vettool="$(which momovet)" ./...
```

It also runs standalone: `momovet ./...`.

To embed it in your own multichecker, import `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/momovet` and use its `Analyzer` variable.

## Limits

The analyzer does not follow assignments. A `var` that holds a literal is reported, even a package-level one that is never reassigned: this is a false positive by design, so declare it as a `const`. It checks the call site only, so SQL built in one function and passed through another is reported where it reaches a raw-SQL function.


# Source: capabilities.md

What Momo supports, per database. The status of each database and the dialect
flags below are generated from the code: see [MySQL and MariaDB](mysql.md),
[migrations](migrations.md#3a-sqlite) and [vectors](vectors.md) for the details
behind them.

<!-- generated:status -->

<!-- Generated by go generate ./internal/gendocs from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

A database is usable when a driver package for it exists under `driver/`:

- PostgreSQL: usable through `driver/pgxdriver` (vector builders: yes). Migrations: `migrate/postgres`, run by `momo migrate`.
- SQLite: usable through `driver/sqlitedriver` (needs cgo, not on Windows, vector builders: yes) and `driver/sqlitepure` (vector builders: no). Migrations: `migrate/sqlite`, library only (`momo migrate` does not select it).
- MySQL and MariaDB: usable through `driver/mysqldriver` (vector storage and builders depend on the server version). Migrations: `migrate/mysql`, library only (`momo migrate` does not select it).

<!-- /generated:status -->

Legend: yes = implemented for PostgreSQL and covered by the integration suite
(`make test-integration-postgres`, which also runs every dialect-neutral test
on SQLite through `testopen.Each`). no = not provided. `ErrUnsupported` = the
call exists and fails with `momo.ErrUnsupported`.

## Getting connected

Imports: `github.com/azrtydxb/momo` (core), `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/driver/pgxdriver`
(PostgreSQL driver), `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/vector` for vector types and
`github.com/azrtydxb/momo/vecop` for the vector distance builders.

Open a pool and wrap it, as the README does (the caller closes the pool):

<!-- docscheck:fragment -->

```go
pool, err := pgxdriver.NewPool(ctx, url) // (ctx, string) (*pgxpool.Pool, error)
if err != nil { return err }
defer pool.Close()
db := momo.New(pgxdriver.New(pool)) // New(pool, opts ...Option) momo.Driver
```

DSN: `postgres://user:password@host:5432/dbname?sslmode=verify-full`. Use
`sslmode=disable` for local development only.

With `database/sql`: `pgxdriver.FromConnConfig(cfg *pgx.ConnConfig, opts ...Option) (*sql.DB, momo.Driver)`
or `pgxdriver.FromSQLDB(db *sql.DB)`. These have no Batch or COPY path.

Existing transactions: `db.AdoptTx(pgxdriver.SQLTx(sqlTx))` and
`db.AdoptTx(pgxdriver.PgxTx(pgxTx))` run momo inside a transaction the caller
began (Commit and Rollback return `ErrAdoptedTx`; the caller finishes it), and
`pgxdriver.UnwrapSQLTx(tx)` or `pgxdriver.UnwrapPgxTx(tx)` give legacy code the
`*sql.Tx` or `pgx.Tx` behind a `*momo.Tx`. Committing or rolling back the
unwrapped handle of a momo-begun transaction is not allowed; momo still owns it.
An adopted `pgx.Tx` keeps Batch (relation loading pipelines) and `COPY`; `COPY`
is always binary, so vector columns need the pgvector codec on the caller's
connection (`ConfigureVectors` on the pool, or your own AfterConnect). An
adopted `*sql.Tx` has neither. `PgxTx` accepts the options of `New`; an exec
mode that `WithExecMode` rejects makes every statement, batch and `COPY` on the
adopted transaction return `ErrUnsupported`, as with `New`.

Vectors need the pgvector `vector` extension in the database. The generated
migration emits `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "vector"` when a model has a
vector column (see `vectors.md`).

PgBouncer (transaction pooling): `pgxdriver.New` defaults to
`pgx.QueryExecModeExec` (unnamed statements), and the CI PgBouncer tests open a
pool and use `New(pool)` with that default, so no setting is needed. With
`FromConnConfig` the exec mode is `cfg.DefaultQueryExecMode`, which pgx
defaults to `CacheStatement` (not PgBouncer-safe), so set
`cfg.DefaultQueryExecMode = pgx.QueryExecModeExec` before calling it; its
`opts` have no effect.

## Dialect and driver status

<!-- generated:capabilities -->

<!-- Generated by go generate ./internal/gendocs from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

| Item                             | PostgreSQL                                       | SQLite                                     | MySQL                | MariaDB              |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | -------------------- | -------------------- |
| Usable (a driver package exists) | yes                                              | yes                                        | yes                  | yes                  |
| Driver package                   | `driver/pgxdriver`                               | `driver/sqlitedriver`, `driver/sqlitepure` | `driver/mysqldriver` | `driver/mysqldriver` |
| Migration dialect                | `migrate/postgres`                               | `migrate/sqlite`                           | `migrate/mysql`      | `migrate/mysql`      |
| `momo migrate` runs it           | yes                                              | no                                         | no                   | no                   |
| `MaxParams`                      | 65535                                            | 32766                                      | 65535                | 65535                |
| `Returning`                      | yes                                              | yes                                        | no                   | no                   |
| `InsertReturning`                | no                                               | no                                         | no                   | yes                  |
| `OnConflict`                     | yes                                              | yes                                        | no                   | no                   |
| `OnDuplicateKey`                 | no                                               | no                                         | yes                  | yes                  |
| `Locking`                        | yes                                              | no                                         | yes                  | yes                  |
| `NullsOrdering`                  | yes                                              | yes                                        | no                   | no                   |

| `IsolationLevels`                | yes                                              | no                                         | yes                  | yes                  |
| `TransactionalDDL`               | yes                                              | yes                                        | no                   | no                   |
| `ILike`                          | yes                                              | no                                         | no                   | no                   |
| `Merge`                          | yes                                              | no                                         | no                   | no                   |
| `WindowFunctions`                | yes                                              | yes                                        | yes                  | yes                  |
| `Vector.Storage`                 | yes                                              | yes                                        | yes                  | yes                  |
| `Vector.Metrics`                 | `l2`, `ip`, `cosine`, `l1`, `hamming`, `jaccard` | `l2`, `l1`, `cosine`, `hamming`            | none                 | `l2`, `cosine`       |
| `Vector.Indexes`                 | `hnsw`, `ivfflat`                                | none                                       | none                 | `vector`             |

<!-- /generated:capabilities -->

The vector rows are dialect metadata. What a MySQL-family server can do depends
on its version: MySQL 8.4 has no `VECTOR` type, MySQL 9.x stores vectors without
a distance function, and MariaDB 11.8 has L2 and cosine distance functions. See
[MySQL and MariaDB](mysql.md) and [vectors](vectors.md).

## JSON operators and date and time expressions

<!-- generated:features -->

<!-- Generated by go generate ./internal/gendocs from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

| Feature                           | API                                                                                                                                                                                    | PostgreSQL | SQLite                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | MySQL / MariaDB                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| JSON operators on `types.JSON[T]` | `jsonop.Text`, `jsonop.Path`, `jsonop.Contains`, `jsonop.HasKey`                                                                                                                       | yes        | `jsonop.Text`, `jsonop.Path` and `jsonop.HasKey` run on both SQLite drivers; a JSON boolean extracts as `1` or `0`; `jsonop.Contains` is `ErrUnsupported`, since `json_each` cannot express the recursive `@>` rule                                                                                   | SQL is golden-tested only; no integration test runs it against a MySQL or MariaDB server                                         |
| Date and time expressions         | `timeop.Extract`, `timeop.AtTimeZone`, `timeop.Trunc`, `timeop.Now`, `timeop.CurrentTimestamp`, `timeop.IntervalOf`, `timeop.IntervalExpr`, `timeop.AddInterval`, `timeop.SubInterval` | yes        | every `timeop.ExtractField`, `timeop.TruncUnit`, interval and `timeop.Now` run on both SQLite drivers; month arithmetic overflows into the next month (Jan 31 plus a month is Mar 2 or 3, where PostgreSQL and MySQL clamp); `timeop.Now` is millisecond text; `timeop.AtTimeZone` is PostgreSQL only | SQL is golden-tested only; no integration test runs it against a MySQL or MariaDB server; `timeop.AtTimeZone` is PostgreSQL only |

## Core queries

| Feature                                                           | PostgreSQL                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | SQLite / MySQL                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | API                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Insert one / many                                                 | yes                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (`suite.RunAll`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `Insert[T]`: `.Model(&m)`, `.Models(ms)`, `.Values`, `.ValuesRows`, `.Omit`, `.Exec`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Insert chunking over the bind limit                               | yes, atomic (one transaction, or a savepoint inside a `Tx`); `MaxParams` 65535                                                                                                                                                  | SQLite: yes, covered by the integration tests that run on SQLite; MySQL: not covered by a MySQL integration test yet                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `Models` + `Exec`; `WithMaxParams(n)` lowers the limit; one row over the limit: `ErrLimitExceeded`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Insert as one `unnest` statement                                  | yes: `InsertQuery[T].Unnest()` sends one array parameter per column, so the bind count does not grow with the rows and `MaxParams` / `WithMaxParams` do not apply (one statement, no chunking)                                  | `ErrUnsupported` on SQLite and MySQL                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `Model` / `Models` only (`InsertQuery.Values`, `InsertQuery.ValuesRows` and `FromSelect` give `ErrValidation`); needs the table schema in the generated metadata, or `ErrValidation`. Int, float, bool, string, `time.Time` and `[]byte` columns bind as typed arrays (`[]*T` when a value is NULL); other element types (uuid, json, decimal, named enums) fall back to `[]any`, which pgx may reject, so use plain `Models` for such a model. `OnConflict`, `Upsert` and `Returning` work as for `Models`; interceptors, `BeforeInsert`, field validators, automatic timestamps and id generators run as for `Models`. A `FlagSensitive` column's array is `RedactedArg` in `QueryEvent.Args`. Not the package-level FROM source `momo.Unnest` |
| Select                                                            | yes                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (`suite.RunAll`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `Select[T]`: `Where`, `OrderBy`, `Limit`, `Offset`, `Distinct`, `All`, `One`, `First`, `Count`, `Exists`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Update, Delete                                                    | yes; without `Where` they fail with `ErrUnfilteredMutation` unless `.AllRows()`                                                                                                                                                 | SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (`suite.RunAll`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `UpdateQuery[T].Set(...)`, `Delete[T]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| UPDATE ... FROM, DELETE ... USING, WITH on DML, DML as a CTE body | yes: `UpdateQuery.From`, `DeleteQuery.Using`, `InsertQuery.With` / `InsertQuery.WithRecursive` on `InsertQuery`, `UpdateQuery` and `DeleteQuery`, and an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE with `Returning` as a `SelectQuery.With` body | SQLite: `UPDATE ... FROM` and WITH before any DML yes, `DELETE ... USING` and a data-modifying CTE body `ErrUnsupported`. MySQL and MariaDB: multi-table `UPDATE t, src SET ...` and `DELETE t FROM t, src`; WITH before UPDATE and DELETE on MySQL only (MariaDB `ErrUnsupported`, not verified); WITH before INSERT and a data-modifying CTE body `ErrUnsupported` | `From` / `Using` take a table, `momo.CTE` or `momo.FromSubquery`; the soft-delete filter and interceptors do not apply to that source. With `From` or `Using`, `Where` must reference the target table or the statement is `ErrUnfilteredMutation` unless `AllRows`. A WITH on a chunked bulk insert or on `BulkUpdate` is `ErrValidation`; an INSERT CTE body over the parameter limit is `ErrLimitExceeded`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Soft delete                                                       | yes                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (`suite.RunAll`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `SoftDelete`, `ForceDelete`, `WithDeleted`, `OnlyDeleted`; field tag `soft_delete:`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Optimistic lock, automatic timestamps                             | yes                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (`suite.RunAll`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | version column (`ErrOptimisticLock`); `created_at`, `updated_at` tags                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Typed predicates                                                  | yes                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | SQLite: yes, covered by the integration tests that run on SQLite; MySQL: not covered by a MySQL integration test yet                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | generated columns: `Eq`, `In`, `IsNull`, `Lt`, ...; `And`, `Or`, `Not`, `Like` and `ILike` (always `ESCAPE '!'`, see `EscapeLike`), `ContainsLiteral`, `Exists`; `In` over the bind limit is `ErrValidation`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Array columns and operators                                       | yes: `[]string` maps to `text[]`, also `[]int16`, `[]int32`, `[]int64`, `[]bool`, `[]float32`, `[]float64`, `[]types.UUID` (`uuid[]`); one bind per slice                                                                       | `ErrUnsupported` at build time                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `arrayop.Contains` (`@>`), `arrayop.ContainedBy` (`<@`), `arrayop.Overlaps` (`&&`), `arrayop.AnyOf` (`= ANY`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Joins                                                             | yes                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (`suite.RunAll`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `Join`, `LeftJoin`, `CrossJoin`, `From`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Aggregates, `GroupBy`, `Having`                                   | yes                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (`suite.RunAll`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `CountAll`, `CountOf`, `CountDistinct`, `Sum`, `Avg`, `Min`, `Max`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Projections (non-model result types)                              | yes                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | SQLite: yes, covered by the integration tests that run on SQLite; MySQL: not covered by a MySQL integration test yet                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | struct embedding `momo.Projection` with `Columns(...)`, or generic tuple rows `Row1` to `Row10`; metadata is generated; soft-deleted rows of the `From` table are filtered                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Serial ids                                                        | yes: `serial` tag, `smallserial`, `serial` or `bigserial` by Go int width                                                                                                                                                       | refused                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | omitted from inserts and read back with `RETURNING`; a `FromSelect` into the table cannot supply ids                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Keyset pagination                                                 | yes, non-nullable keys only                                                                                                                                                                                                     | SQLite: yes, covered by the integration tests that run on SQLite; MySQL: not covered by a MySQL integration test yet                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `OrderBy(...).After(values...)`; the primary key is appended as tie-breaker; nullable key: `ErrUnsupported`; wrong value count: `ErrValidation`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Streaming                                                         | yes                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | SQLite: yes, covered by the integration tests that run on SQLite; MySQL: not covered by a MySQL integration test yet                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `Each(ctx, fn)`, `Iter(ctx)` (`iter.Seq2`); both `ErrUnsupported` when the query has `Preload`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Raw SQL                                                           | yes                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (`suite.RunAll`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `momo.Exec`, `momo.Scalars`, `momo.Query`, `momo.QueryRows`, `momo.SQL`, `TypedSQL`, `RawSubquery`, `Named`, `In`, `Ident`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `EXPLAIN`                                                         | yes (`EXPLAIN`, never `ANALYZE`)                                                                                                                                                                                                | MySQL: `ErrUnsupported`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `SelectQuery.Explain(ctx)`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `IndexedBy` hint                                                  | `ErrUnsupported`; SQLite syntax, run on SQLite in v0.6.0 through `sqlitedriver`                                                                                                                                                 | MySQL: `ErrUnsupported`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `SelectQuery.IndexedBy` <!-- x-release-please-version -->                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

## Writes, transactions, drivers

| Feature                                    | PostgreSQL                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | SQLite / MySQL                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RETURNING`                                | yes (`Returning: true`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | MySQL: no; MariaDB: `INSERT ... RETURNING` only (`InsertReturning`)                                                                                                                                                                                                        | `.Returning(cols...)`, `.ReturningAll()` on insert, update, delete; read with `.Rows(ctx)`. Identity read-back in `CreateGraph` needs it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `INSERT ... SELECT`                        | yes: `InsertQuery[T].FromSelect` with `SelectExprs` (FROM-less or one source, with `Where`) or `Select[T]` as the source; composes with `OnConflict`, `Returning`, `Upsert[T]`                                                                | SQLite yes (`WHERE true` is added to a `SelectExprs` or `Select[T]` source with FROM and no WHERE before `ON CONFLICT`); MySQL plain insert only (no `ON CONFLICT`; FROM-less with WHERE renders `FROM DUAL`)                                                              | Target columns are explicit typed columns of T; a select-list count mismatch is `ErrValidation`. No model hooks, automatic timestamps, Go-side defaults or validators are applied: list those columns yourself. The soft-delete filter on a `SelectExprs` source needs a `TableRef` that carries the soft-delete marker.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Upsert / `ON CONFLICT`                     | yes (`OnConflict: true`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | MySQL and MariaDB: `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` through the same calls, with the conflict target limited to the only unique key of the table (otherwise `ErrUnsupported`); see [mysql.md](mysql.md)                                                                           | `Upsert[T]` (target = primary key) or `InsertQuery[T].OnConflict(cols...).DoNothing()` / `.DoUpdate(assigns...)` with `SetExcluded`. Upsert neither advances nor checks the version column. `OnConflict(...).Where(preds)` (partial-index target) and `.DoUpdate(...).Where(preds)` (conditional update, `col.Excluded()`): PostgreSQL yes; SQLite: bool, integer, finite float and string values in the target predicate render inline so they match the index expression (golden-tested and run against a real SQLite partial unique index written as `WHERE live = 1`; the values show up in logs and traces; write index literals as Momo renders them, integers as `2` and floats in plain decimal with `.0` for whole numbers for magnitudes from 1e-6 up to 1e21 and exponent form (`1e-07`, `1e+21`) outside that range, otherwise use `momo.SQL`), any other value or `Excluded()` there is `ErrValidation`; MySQL `ErrUnsupported`. |
| Graph writes                               | yes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | SQLite: yes, covered by the integration tests that run on SQLite; MySQL: not covered by a MySQL integration test yet                                                                                                                                                       | `CreateGraph`, `FindOrCreate` (needs `ON CONFLICT`), `UpsertByPK`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `Merge`, `BulkUpdate`, `Truncate`          | yes: `Merge` is PostgreSQL 15 or later and `.Returning` needs 17 or later (`ErrUnsupported` on an older server or a driver without `ServerVersioner`); `BulkUpdate` updates only the listed keys (PostgreSQL); `Truncate` is `TRUNCATE TABLE` | `Merge` and `BulkUpdate`: `ErrUnsupported`. `Truncate`: SQLite runs `DELETE FROM` and resets the autoincrement counter; MySQL runs `TRUNCATE TABLE` (refused inside a transaction)                                                                                         | `Merge` returns `ErrValidation` when an interceptor adds predicates (deny the kind instead). `Truncate` runs interceptors with the kind `truncate`, has no `RESTART IDENTITY` or `CASCADE`, and is refused inside a MySQL transaction. `Merge` does not run field validators on the inserted values                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Bulk `COPY`                                | yes: `InsertQuery[T].Copy` (after `Omit`, with the models as its argument) on the pgx driver; also `momo.CopierOf(querier)` for the driver call                                                                                               | SQLite and MySQL: `Copy` returns `ErrUnsupported` (neither `sqlitedriver` nor `mysqldriver` has a `Copier`)                                                                                                                                                                | `Copy` runs the insert interceptors (deny only) and `BeforeInsert` over a copy of the models; it skips `OnConflict`, `Returning` and chunking, and it counts as a write for `NewUnitOfWork`. On a `*DB` with `WithImplicitTx` it runs in its own transaction; on a pinned handle with `WithTxSetup` it fails closed. Not available through `FromSQLDB`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Batch (several statements, one round trip) | driver level: `momo.BatcherOf(querier)`; relation loading uses it automatically                                                                                                                                                               | SQLite: no (`sqlitedriver` has no `Batcher`); MySQL: no (`mysqldriver` has no `Batcher`)                                                                                                                                                                                   | not available through `FromSQLDB`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Transactions                               | yes: `db.Tx(ctx, opts, fn)`, `db.Begin`; read uncommitted, read committed, repeatable read, serializable; read-only                                                                                                                           | SQLite and MySQL: commit, rollback and panic cases run in the shared suite (`suite.RunAll`); SQLite accepts the default and serializable isolation only (other levels `ErrUnsupported`) and runs read-only transactions through `PRAGMA query_only` (`sqlitedriver` tests) | any other `sql.IsolationLevel`: `ErrUnsupported` (Op "begin")                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Savepoints                                 | yes: `Tx.Savepoint`, `RollbackTo`, `Release`                                                                                                                                                                                                  | SQLite and MySQL: yes, covered by the shared suite (`suite.RunAll`)                                                                                                                                                                                                        | a dialect without savepoints: `ErrUnsupported` (Op "savepoint")                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Pinned connection                          | yes: `db.OnConn(pc)`                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | SQLite and MySQL: the drivers implement `Pinner` (driver tests); `db.OnConn` itself is exercised by a MySQL test (generated keys) and not by a SQLite test                                                                                                                 | no transactions on a pinned `*DB`: `Begin`, `Tx`, `Replace` and `CreateGraph` fail with `ErrUnsupported` (Op "begin"), chunked `Insert` with Op "insert"; `Link`, `Unlink` and `Count` work                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `SET col = DEFAULT`, `VALUES (DEFAULT)`    | yes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | SQLite: no `DEFAULT` in `VALUES`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | a multi-row insert that is default in some rows only fails with `ErrUnsupported` where the dialect cannot express it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

## Row locking, CTEs, subqueries, window functions

| Feature                                                                    | PostgreSQL                                                                                                                                             | SQLite / MySQL                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | API                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
