| `LoadPerParentLimit`                                          | belongs-to or has-one relation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `Link`, `Unlink`, `Replace`, `Count`                          | belongs-to relation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Vector builders                                               | metric the dialect lacks (inner product and Jaccard on SQLite), or the driver reports `Vectors: false`                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `vecsearch.Apply`, `vecsearch.With`                           | pgvector missing or older than 0.8.0 when an iterative, `max_scan_tuples`, `scan_mem_multiplier` or `max_probes` field is set; any non-`ExactSearch` field on SQLite; transaction-scoped settings on a non-PostgreSQL dialect                                                                                              |
| `SelectQuery.Explain`                                         | MySQL and MariaDB                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Migration inspect or apply                                    | missing extension (for example `vector`): the error names it; unsupported object on inspect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `pgxdriver.WithExecMode`                                      | simple protocol or any unlisted mode: every query returns it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `pgxdriver.FromSQLDB`                                         | nil `db`, or a `db` not backed by the pgx stdlib driver (every Query, Exec, Begin and Pin then fails). A valid `FromSQLDB` driver can Pin, but the pinned connection has no Batch or COPY                                                                                                                                  |
| Generator type mapping                                        | Go type with no SQL mapping on the dialect (`gen/typemap`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Batch, `COPY`                                                 | a pinned connection without a batch or COPY path (Op "batch", "copy"); `WithExecMode` differing from the connection's default exec mode makes the pgx batch fail (Op "batch"). Relation loading falls back to sequential on its own in both cases; a `FromSQLDB` pinned connection has no `Batcher` and loads sequentially |


# Source: PERFORMANCE.md

# Performance

Budgets are measured, never aspirational. This page starts with the hook
overhead budget that `TestSelectNoHooksAllocBudget` enforces. The `bench/`
module (a separate Go module, so GORM, Ent and Bun never enter the library's
import graph) holds the comparison workloads; its methodology, versions and
regression policy are added here as the suite lands.

## Hook overhead budget

A primary-key lookup on a database with no hooks registered must not allocate
more than the budget below. The figure is `allocs/op` of
`BenchmarkSelectNoHooks`, measured by the `TestSelectNoHooksAllocBudget` run in CI. The full CI matrix
(Go 1.26 and 1.27, PostgreSQL 16 and 17 with pgvector 0.8.7) measures the same
32, so one budget covers every combination. The test fails when the measured
value rises above the budget, so an allocation added to the disabled-hook path
is caught. Lower the budget in the same change whenever the path gets cheaper.

| Benchmark                        | Budget |
| -------------------------------- | ------ |
| BenchmarkSelectNoHooks allocs/op | 32     |

To reproduce, run `make db-up`, then `make bench-hooks`. The benchmark opens a database, so it only compiles with the `integration` build tag and `make bench-smoke` skips it; the `bench-module` CI job runs `make bench-hooks` against the pgvector service.

## Streaming memory bound

`SelectQuery.Each` hands rows to a callback one at a time and must not buffer
the result set. `TestStreamingBoundedMemory` iterates one million rows with
`Each`, reads the heap after a forced collection every 100000 rows, and fails
when the heap has grown by more than the bound below, so an `Each` that
collects the rows first is caught.

| Limit                             | Value |
| --------------------------------- | ----- |
| Streaming heap growth bound (MiB) | 16    |

## Comparison suite

The `bench/` module compares Momo with handwritten pgx and database/sql, GORM,
Ent and Bun on one PostgreSQL server. Every operation is defined once in
`bench/workload` and each library implements it in `bench/adapters`; the
equivalence test `TestBenchEquivalence` fails when an adapter returns different
rows than the handwritten pgx reference or leaves different state after a
write, so a workload whose SQL meaning differs between libraries cannot be
published.

### Methodology

- Identical pool settings for every adapter: 16 connections, one hour
  connection lifetime. The native pgx path uses the statement cache; the other
  libraries run on the pgx standard library driver.
- GORM runs with `SkipDefaultTransaction`, as Momo adds no implicit
  transaction. Bun runs on the same pgx standard library `database/sql` handle
  as Ent and GORM, so the comparison isolates the ORM layer. No library cache
  is enabled.
- The data is deterministic: a fixed seed, 200 customers with 5 orders each.
  `ANALYZE` runs after seeding.
- ORM-only microbenchmarks report p50, p95 and p99 per call beside allocations,
  for six operations over all six libraries. A mixed read and write workload
  with concurrency and the bulk insert paths have their own runners.
- Bulk insert compares chunked VALUES, COPY and Momo's `Unnest`, one statement
  with one array parameter per column, at 1000, 10000 and 40000 rows.
- Vector search is compared at equal recall: a sweep picks the smallest
  `hnsw.ef_search` whose recall at 10 reaches 0.95 against exact search, and both
  the Momo builder and the handwritten statement then run at that setting.
- Generated-code size and compile cost of the benchmark models are measured by
  `bench/codesize`.

### Pinned versions

The module versions are pinned in `bench/go.mod`; each run records them in
`versions.txt` and `env.json`, together with the Go toolchain, the machine, the
PostgreSQL version and the pgvector version. The database image is
`pgvector/pgvector:0.8.7-pg17`.

### Reproducing a run

`make db-up` starts PostgreSQL with pgvector. Then `make bench` runs the whole
suite ten times per benchmark and writes `bench/results/` under a directory named
by UTC time, operating system and architecture, with `env.json`, `versions.txt`,
`codesize.json`, `raw.txt` and `summary.txt`, plus `vector-encoding.txt` (the
`BenchmarkVectorEncoding` run of text against binary pgx vector codecs) when a
database is configured. `make bench-suite-smoke` runs one
iteration of everything and is what CI uses. `make bench-generate` regenerates
the Momo metadata and the Ent client.

### Regression policy

- Timings are judged only on a dedicated machine: a regression is flagged when
  benchstat reports a change above 10 percent with p below 0.05 across two
  consecutive full runs. Shared CI runners are too noisy for timings, so CI never
  gates on them.
- Allocation counts are deterministic, so CI gates them: the `bench-module`
  job of `ci.yml` and `ci-agent.yml` runs `make bench-gate`, which runs the
  allocation benchmarks, compares allocs/op with `bench/baseline/allocs.txt`
  using benchstat and fails above 5 percent with p below 0.05. The gate runs in
  that one job only, against the PostgreSQL service the job already starts, so
  a pull request pays for one database job and not a second one. The recipe
  runs under bash with pipefail, and `benchgate` exits 2 (never 0) when the new
  run has no allocs/op rows or lacks a benchmark that the baseline has, so a
  run that never happened cannot pass. `make bench-gate` runs the same
  comparison locally and `make bench-baseline` rewrites the baseline.
- Budgets are the median of the reference run plus 10 percent and are reviewed
  on every full run.

### Status of the published numbers

No full run on a dedicated machine has been committed yet, so this page records
no comparative timings. The only budget in force is the hook overhead budget
above, which CI enforces. Timing figures will be added from the stored
`bench/results/` run, never from a shared runner.

# Supported versions

What Momo v0.6.0 is built and tested against. "Tested" means a job in <!-- x-release-please-version -->
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs it. Anything not listed there is untested, not
necessarily broken.

## Module

| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| Version     | v0.6.0 (tags use a `v` prefix) <!-- x-release-please-version -->           |
| Install     | `go get github.com/azrtydxb/momo@v0.6.0` <!-- x-release-please-version --> |
| CLI         | `go run github.com/azrtydxb/momo/cmd/momo` (or `go install` the same path) |

## Databases

<!-- generated:status -->

<!-- Generated by go generate ./internal/gendocs from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

A database is usable when a driver package for it exists under `driver/`:

- PostgreSQL: usable through `driver/pgxdriver` (vector builders: yes). Migrations: `migrate/postgres`, run by `momo migrate`.
- SQLite: usable through `driver/sqlitedriver` (needs cgo, not on Windows, vector builders: yes) and `driver/sqlitepure` (vector builders: no). Migrations: `migrate/sqlite`, library only (`momo migrate` does not select it).
- MySQL and MariaDB: usable through `driver/mysqldriver` (vector storage and builders depend on the server version). Migrations: `migrate/mysql`, library only (`momo migrate` does not select it).

<!-- /generated:status -->

Servers the integration jobs run against: PostgreSQL 16 and 17 with pgvector (see below), and MySQL 8.4, MySQL 9.7 and MariaDB 11.8 for the MySQL driver. Vector support on the MySQL family depends on the server version: MySQL 8.4 has no `VECTOR` type, MySQL 9.x stores vectors but has no distance function, and MariaDB 11.8 has L2 and cosine distance functions (see [MySQL and MariaDB](mysql.md)).

## Stability policy

| Item                | Statement                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pre-1.0             | the README states: "v0.6.0, pre-v1, with no compatibility promise between releases" <!-- x-release-please-version -->                                                                                                         |
| Versioning          | release-please with `bump-minor-pre-major: true` and Conventional Commits; breaking changes are marked `feat!:` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer (CONTRIBUTING)                                                                 |
| Deprecation process | none documented                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Security fixes      | latest minor only (`SECURITY.md`)                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Pin your dependency | use an exact version in `go.mod` and read `CHANGELOG.md` before each upgrade                                                                                                                                                  |
| Generated code      | regenerate with `momo generate` after every upgrade; generated files carry only a format number in their header, so an upgrade rewrites them only when the generated code changes; `momo generate --check` reports stale ones |


# Source: upgrading.md

# Upgrading

Momo is pre-v1 and makes no compatibility promise between releases; see the
[stability policy](supported-versions.md#stability-policy). Read this page and
the `CHANGELOG.md` entry of a release before you upgrade, and expect that
later releases can break more.

## Upgrading to 0.6.0

### The Using and From guard is stricter

`UpdateQuery.From` and `DeleteQuery.Using` refuse a statement whose `Where`
does not reference the target table, with `ErrUnfilteredMutation`. The guard
now follows `Or`, `Not` and `JoinSQL`: an `Or` counts only when every branch
references the target, an `And` when any term does, and `Not` swaps the two
rules. `JoinSQL` with `AND` or `OR` follows the same rules, and `JoinSQL` with
any other separator never counts. Statements that passed in 0.5.0 and are now
refused: `Where(momo.Or(PostCols.ID.Eq(1), SrcCols.Title.Eq("x")))`, where one
`Or` branch is off the target, and
`Where(momo.Not(momo.And(PostCols.ID.Eq(1), SrcCols.Title.Eq("x"))))`, which is
an `Or` of negations.

Add a condition on the target to every branch, or call `AllRows()` when the
statement is meant to touch every row. The guard checks that the condition
references the target, not that it restricts it: `t.id = t.id` still passes.

### OpenAPI error bodies use the key `error`

The OpenAPI document and the generated handlers now describe and send errors
as `{"error": "<message>"}`. The `Error` schema property was `message` in 0.4.0.
A client that reads `message` from an error response must read `error`. Error
messages are fixed strings: a constraint violation no longer shows the table or
constraint name.

### Generated handlers and servers

The ecosystem generators (`graphql`, `grpc`, `openapi`, enabled in the
`plugins:` section of `momo.yaml`) generate servers that do no authentication
and no authorization. Wrap the `http.ServeMux`, the `grpc.Server` or the
GraphQL handler. Turn off operations of the `openapi` and `grpc` servers with
`ops` or `read_only: true` (the `graphql` plugin has neither option); see the
[capabilities](capabilities.md) page for the options, the error mapping, the
update semantics and the GraphQL limits.

PUT and gRPC Update differ on purpose. An OpenAPI PUT must carry every required
property and writes only the properties it carries, so a property it leaves out
keeps whatever value the database has, including one a concurrent request just
wrote. A gRPC Update has no way to leave a scalar out (a proto3 scalar at its
zero value is a value), so it writes every writable column the message holds;
a vector, a timestamp or a defaulted scalar left unset is not written. Neither
reads the row first and writes it back.

### View models no longer produce a table

A model that embeds `momo.View` maps a view, so the generated schema, and with
it `momo migrate diff`, holds no table for it. A view model gets no
`CREATE TABLE`, and a foreign key never points at it. Declare the view itself
with `c.View` in `MomoConfig`.

The generated servers expose only list and get for a view model: there is no
create, update or delete route, RPC or mutation, and naming a write operation
for a view model in `ops` is a generator error.

If you add `momo.View` to a model whose table really exists in the database,
`momo migrate diff` now plans a `DROP TABLE` for that table (AutoMigrate skips
it). Review the diff before you apply it.

`momo.RefreshMaterializedView` refreshes a materialized view (PostgreSQL only).

### OpenAPI input and output schemas

The OpenAPI document now has two schemas per model. `<Model>` (for example
`Document`) is the output: every column, with the not-null columns, the key
included, listed in `required`. A client generator now types `id` as required
on a response. `<Model>Input` (`DocumentInput`) is new and is what a create and
a PUT take: only the writable properties, so it has no key and no read-only,
identity or serial column, and its `required` list is what it was on `<Model>`
in 0.5.0 (not null, no database default). Every response keeps referencing
`<Model>`; the request bodies of create and PUT now reference `<Model>Input`.
A client generated from the old document sends the same JSON and keeps working;
regenerate it to get the new types. A model whose name plus `Input` is also a
model name (`Doc` and `DocInput`) is a generator diagnostic.

The gRPC messages are unchanged: a model message is still what a client sends
and receives. The field comments in the `.proto` file say which fields a request
ignores (the key on Create, read-only columns on Create and Update, and the
version, soft-delete and timestamp columns on Update).

### Error hook and cancellation codes

The `openapi` and `grpc` plugins take the option `on_error`, the name of a Go
function in the generated package with the signature
`func(ctx context.Context, op string, err error)`. The generated code calls it
once for every error it answers from a statement (a database error, a missing
row, a cancelled context), with the operation (the `operationId` for OpenAPI,
for example `getDocument`; `DocumentService.Get` for gRPC) and the original
error, before it writes the fixed message. Log, count or trace the error there.
A panic in the hook is recovered, so it cannot stop the request from being
answered. The `openapi` option needs `handlers: true`, because only the
generated handlers call the hook. Without the option nothing changes.

A request whose context was cancelled is now answered 499 (OpenAPI), `Canceled`
(gRPC) and `CANCELED` (GraphQL) with a fixed message, and one whose deadline
passed 504, `DeadlineExceeded` and `CANCELED`. These were 500 and `Internal`
before. A client or proxy that retries on 500 will no longer retry them.

## Upgrading to 0.5.0

### Regenerating with `--from-db` after the `dbdefault` tag

`momo generate --from-db` now adds the `dbdefault` tag to every NOT NULL
PostgreSQL column whose default is computed (`gen_random_uuid()`, `now()`,
`CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, `nextval(...)` and other function calls). A Go zero value
is no longer written for such a column: `InsertQuery.Model` and `InsertQuery.Models` leave it out,
the database default applies, and the value is read back with `RETURNING`.
Review the regenerated models: a `bool`, number, empty string or zero time in
such a field can no longer be written explicitly through `Model` (use `InsertQuery.Values`
or remove the tag), and a plain MySQL database refuses a zero value with
`ErrUnsupported` because it cannot read the default back. Hand-written models
are unaffected until they add the tag. See "Database defaults" in the
[AI guide](ai-guide.md).

### Advisory string helpers take options

`advisory.XactLockString` and `advisory.TryXactLockString` take a trailing
`...advisory.Option` (for `advisory.Hash64`). A call site is unchanged, but
the function types changed: code that assigns one of these functions to a
variable or field of the old func type no longer compiles. Wrap the call in a
closure instead.

### Model hook methods are now wired by `momo generate`

`momo generate` detects methods named `BeforeInsert`, `BeforeUpdate`,
`BeforeDelete` and `AfterLoad` on a model and fills `Meta.Hooks` with them.
Two behaviors change for an existing model after you regenerate:

- A method with one of these names and the exact signature
  `func(context.Context) error` now runs: before inserts, updates and deletes,
  and after loads. Before, such a method was never called. If you had a method
  with a hook name that was meant as plain code, rename it before you
  regenerate.
- A method with one of these names and any other signature makes
  `momo generate` fail with a positioned diagnostic
  (`hook BeforeInsert on Doc must have signature func(context.Context) error`),
  and a hook-named method on a projection is a diagnostic as well (a projection
  runs no hooks). Fix the signature or rename the method.

If you set `Meta.Hooks` by hand in a hand-written `Meta`, nothing changes.
Generated files are rewritten by `momo generate`; the `Hooks:` field appears
only for models that have a hook method.

### View models

A model that embeds `momo.View` (new) is marked as a view. Its writes fail with
`ErrValidation`. Existing models are unaffected unless you add the marker.

## Upgrading to 0.4.0

Release 0.4.0 moves feature-specific helpers out of the root package `momo`
into subpackages. Every move is a source break: the old identifier is gone and
the new one lives under a new import path. The release notes are the 0.4.0
entry of the [changelog](https://github.com/azrtydxb/momo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

Why there is no alias: a Go method lives in the package of its receiver type,
and the subpackages import `momo`, so `momo` cannot import them back to keep
the old names. A move therefore deletes the old identifier outright.

### Identifier table

One row per moved identifier. When a method became a function, the old name is
the method and the new name is the function, which takes the former receiver
as an argument.

| Old identifier                      | New import path                      | New identifier                    |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| `momo.ArrayContains`                | `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/arrayop`   | `arrayop.Contains`                |
| `momo.ArrayContainedBy`             | `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/arrayop`   | `arrayop.ContainedBy`             |
| `momo.ArrayOverlaps`                | `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/arrayop`   | `arrayop.Overlaps`                |
| `momo.AnyOf`                        | `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/arrayop`   | `arrayop.AnyOf`                   |

### Rewrite recipe

1. Commit your work first, because the next steps edit files in place, then
   fetch the release: `go get github.com/azrtydxb/momo@v0.4.0`.
2. Save the raw markdown of this page (not the rendered HTML) as `upgrading.md`
   in your module root and run the block below from there. It turns the table
   into `gofmt -r` rules and applies them to the Go files that import
   `github.com/azrtydxb/momo` by that exact path, skipping `vendor/`. It
   rewrites the rows of plain identifiers (functions, types and constants),
   stops with an error when it finds no file or generates no rule, and does not
   touch a file that imports momo under an alias or with a dot import; the
   compiler lists what is left there.

   ```sh
   files=$(grep -rl --include='*.go' 'github.com/azrtydxb/momo"' . | grep -v /vendor/)
   rules=$(awk -F'`' 'NF == 7 && $1 ~ /^\| *$/ && $2 ~ /^momo\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$/ { printf "gofmt -r \"%s -> %s\" -w \"$@\"\n", $2, $6 }' upgrading.md)
   [ -n "$files" ] || { echo "no Go file imports momo" >&2; exit 1; }
   [ -n "$rules" ] || { echo "no rules: upgrading.md must be the raw markdown of this page" >&2; exit 1; }
   echo "$rules" | sh -s -- $files
   ```

3. Rewrite the `momo.Tx.*` and `momo.DB.*` rows by hand, because the receiver
   moves into the argument list: `recv.Old(ctx, args)` becomes
   `pkg.New(ctx, recv, args)`. A `DB` advisory call must pass a transaction
   (see the paragraph on the advisory locks below). The `Validate` method of the old
   `SearchSettings` type is a plain rename: step 2 rewrites the type, and
   `Validate` stays a method of `vecsearch.Settings`.
4. In every file, import each new package that now appears in it (`arrayop.`,
   `fts.`, ...) by the full path in the second column of the table, then build.
   The compiler lists whatever is left.

A row never changes the SQL a query produces; only the Go name and import path
change.

One type gained methods: `sqlfn.CurrentSchemaExpr` now has the comparison and
ordering methods (`Eq`, `In`, `Asc`, ...) the other function results have, so
`sqlfn.CurrentSchema().Eq("app")` compiles, where the old root function's
result had no such method.

The advisory lock methods became functions: `tx.AdvisoryXactLock(ctx, 42)`
is now `advisory.XactLock(ctx, tx, 42)`, and the same for `advisory.XactLockString` and the
`Try` forms. The transaction is the second argument and its type is
`*momo.Tx`. The `DB` methods always returned `momo.ErrValidation`, because a
transaction-scoped lock outside a transaction is released at once; the
functions turn that into a compile error, so a caller that used the `DB` form
must open a transaction with `db.Tx` or `db.Begin`. A dialect other than
PostgreSQL still fails with `momo.ErrUnsupported`.

### What did not move

These stay in `momo`, with the reason:

- `Func` and `FuncExpr`: the generic SQL function escape hatch, which the new
  packages build on.
- `Coalesce`, `Value`, `SQL` and `TypedSQL`: bound-value and raw-fragment
  building blocks of the expression core. `sqlfn.CoalesceExpr` takes expression
  arguments instead.
- The vector column types (`VectorColumn` and its variants): generated code
  references them.
- The hook interfaces (`Hook`, `QueryEvent`, `RelationHook`, `RelationEvent`):
  `DB` stores the hooks and calls them.
- The basic aggregates (`Agg[T]`, `CountAll`, `Sum`, `Avg`, `Min`, `Max`):
  `Having` and select lists are typed on `Agg`.
- `Tx.SetLocal`: a method of `Tx`, and other helpers call it.

# API reference

Every exported identifier of the core package and the feature packages, with the first sentence of its doc comment. Methods are listed as `pkg.Type.Method`. The full text of each comment is on [pkg.go.dev](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/azrtydxb/momo).

## momo

Import path: `github.com/azrtydxb/momo`

| Identifier                             | Kind   | Synopsis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `momo.Agg`                             | type   | Agg is a typed aggregate expression such as COUNT(*) or SUM(col).                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `momo.Agg.As`                          | method | As names the aggregate in a select list: SUM(col) AS name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `momo.Agg.Filter`                      | method | Filter restricts the rows the aggregate sees: COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE p).                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `momo.Agg.Over`                        | method | Over turns an aggregate into a window function: SUM(x) OVER (...).                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `momo.Aliased`                         | type   | Aliased is a select-list item "expr AS alias".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `momo.Aliased.AppendSQL`               | method | AppendSQL writes the expression and its alias to b.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `momo.Aliased.Asc`                     | method | Asc orders by the alias ascending.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `momo.Aliased.Desc`                    | method | Desc orders by the alias descending.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `momo.Aliased.Ref`                     | method | Ref is the typed column through which an outer query reads this alias from a subquery (FromSubquery alias) or CTE (name) called source.                                                                                                                                           |
| `momo.AllowStaleReads`                 | func   | AllowStaleReads returns a context that opts reads of a Replica handle back to the replica even after a write in the same unit of work.                                                                                                                                            |
| `momo.Allowlist`                       | type   | Allowlist maps external names to typed column descriptors.                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `momo.Allowlist.Column`                | method | Column returns the descriptor for name, or a *Error with Kind ErrValidation.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `momo.And`                             | func   | And joins predicates with AND; an empty And is true.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `momo.As`                              | func   | As aliases an expression in a select list: expr AS alias.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `momo.Asc`                             | func   | Asc orders by an arbitrary expression ascending.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `momo.Assignment`                      | type   | Assignment is one explicit column write.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `momo.Assignment.ColumnName`           | method | ColumnName returns the assigned column.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `momo.Association`                     | type   | Association is one relation listed for CreateGraph.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `momo.Avg`                             | func   | Avg is AVG(expr) as float64.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `momo.Batcher`                         | type   | Batcher is implemented by drivers that send several statements in one round trip.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `momo.BatcherOf`                       | func   | BatcherOf returns the Batcher behind q: the driver for a *DB, the transaction for a *Tx.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `momo.Batches`                         | func   | Batches visits every row sq matches in batches of at most n rows, in primary-key order, calling fn for each batch.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `momo.BelongsTo`                       | const  | BelongsTo has its foreign key on the parent; the child is matched by its key.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `momo.Builder`                         | type   | Builder accumulates SQL text and bind arguments for one statement.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `momo.Builder.AppendFilter`            | method | AppendFilter writes " FILTER (WHERE p)" for an aggregate call that was just rendered.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `momo.Builder.Arg`                     | method | Arg appends a bind placeholder and records v as its argument.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `momo.Builder.ArgFor`                  | method | ArgFor binds v like Arg and records it as sensitive when flags carries FlagSensitive, so QueryEvent.Args shows RedactedArg instead of the value.                                                                                                                                  |
| `momo.Builder.Args`                    | method | Args returns the bind arguments built so far.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `momo.Builder.Dialect`                 | method | Dialect returns the dialect being rendered.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `momo.Builder.Err`                     | method | Err returns the first build error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `momo.Builder.ExprFor`                 | method | ExprFor renders e with every argument it binds recorded as sensitive when flags carries FlagSensitive, for an expression compared with or assigned to such a column.                                                                                                              |
| `momo.Builder.Ident`                   | method | Ident appends a quoted identifier.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `momo.Builder.MarkSensitive`           | method | MarkSensitive records that the expression being rendered read a sensitive column, so an enclosing predicate that compares it masks its other operands in hook events.                                                                                                             |
| `momo.Builder.QualifiedIdent`          | method | QualifiedIdent appends qualifier.name, both quoted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `momo.Builder.RenderSensitive`         | method | RenderSensitive renders e and returns flags with FlagSensitive added when e read a sensitive column.                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `momo.Builder.SetErr`                  | method | SetErr records the first build error; rendering continues but the statement will not be executed.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `momo.Builder.String`                  | method | String returns the SQL text built so far.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `momo.Builder.Unsupported`             | method | Unsupported records an ErrUnsupported build error for feature, naming the dialect being rendered.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `momo.Builder.WriteByte`               | method | WriteByte appends a trusted SQL byte.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `momo.Builder.WriteString`             | method | WriteString appends trusted SQL text.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `momo.BulkUpdate`                      | func   | BulkUpdate updates rows of T from a list of rows keyed by key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `momo.CTE`                             | func   | CTE references a common table expression (or any table not described by a model) by name.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `momo.Capabilities`                    | type   | Capabilities describes what a driver can execute beyond the dialect.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `momo.CapabilityReporter`              | type   | CapabilityReporter is implemented by drivers that report driver-level capabilities.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `momo.Coalesce`                        | func   | Coalesce returns the first non-NULL argument.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `momo.Column`                          | type   | Column is a typed column descriptor generated for each model field.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `momo.Column.As`                       | method | As returns the same column qualified by a table alias.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

| `momo.InsertQuery.SQL`                 | method | SQL compiles the statement without executing it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `momo.InsertQuery.Unnest`              | method | Unnest switches a Model or Models insert to one statement that binds one array parameter per column.                                                                                                                                                                              |

INSERT INTO t (cols) SELECT ...                                                                                                                                        |

## dialect

Import path: `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/dialect`

| Identifier                          | Kind   | Synopsis                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `dialect.Dialect`                   | type   | Dialect is immutable after construction and safe for concurrent use.                             |
| `dialect.Dialect.AppendIdent`       | method | AppendIdent appends a quoted identifier.                                                         |
| `dialect.Dialect.AppendPlaceholder` | method | AppendPlaceholder appends the n-th (1-based) bind placeholder.                                   |
| `dialect.Dialect.QuoteIdent`        | method | QuoteIdent returns a quoted identifier.                                                          |
| `dialect.Flavor`                    | type   | Flavor distinguishes servers that share the MySQL dialect.                                       |
| `dialect.FlavorMariaDB`             | const  | FlavorMariaDB is MariaDB.                                                                        |
| `dialect.FlavorMySQL`               | const  | FlavorMySQL is Oracle MySQL.                                                                     |
| `dialect.For`                       | func   | For returns the built-in dialect description for name.                                           |
| `dialect.Metric`                    | type   | Metric names a vector distance metric.                                                           |
| `dialect.MetricCosine`              | const  | <=> on PostgreSQL; vec_distance_cosine on SQLite                                                 |
| `dialect.MetricHamming`             | const  | <~> on PostgreSQL; vec_distance_hamming on SQLite (bit vectors)                                  |
| `dialect.MetricInnerProduct`        | const  | <#> (negative inner product) on PostgreSQL only                                                  |
| `dialect.MetricJaccard`             | const  | <%> on PostgreSQL only                                                                           |
| `dialect.MetricL1`                  | const  | <+> on PostgreSQL; vec_distance_l1 on SQLite                                                     |
| `dialect.MetricL2`                  | const  | <-> on PostgreSQL; vec_distance_l2 on SQLite                                                     |
| `dialect.MySQL`                     | const  | MySQL names the MySQL and MariaDB dialect.                                                       |
| `dialect.MySQLFlavor`               | func   | MySQLFlavor returns the MySQL-family dialect for the given flavor, or nil for an unknown flavor. |
| `dialect.Name`                      | type   | Name identifies a dialect.                                                                       |
| `dialect.Postgres`                  | const  | Postgres names the PostgreSQL dialect.                                                           |
| `dialect.SQLite`                    | const  | SQLite names the SQLite dialect.                                                                 |
| `dialect.VectorCaps`                | type   | VectorCaps describes a dialect's vector support.                                                 |

## schema

Import path: `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/schema`

| Identifier                          | Kind   | Synopsis                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `schema.Check`                      | type   | Check is a CHECK constraint.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `schema.Column`                     | type   | Column is a table column.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `schema.Enum`                       | type   | Enum is a PostgreSQL enum type.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `schema.Equal`                      | func   | Equal reports whether two schemas are equivalent: order of named collections, the Concurrently migration option, and the spelling of types and expressions, and FormatVersion (a file-format marker) are ignored. |
| `schema.ErrInvalidVectorIndex`      | var    | ErrInvalidVectorIndex is wrapped by every ValidateVectorIndex and VectorIndexOpClass error.                                                                                                                       |
| `schema.ErrMissingFormatVersion`    | var    | ErrMissingFormatVersion is returned when a snapshot carries no format_version.                                                                                                                                    |
| `schema.ErrNewerFormat`             | var    | ErrNewerFormat is returned when a snapshot was written by a newer momo.                                                                                                                                           |
| `schema.Extension`                  | type   | Extension is a PostgreSQL extension such as "vector".                                                                                                                                                             |
| `schema.ForeignKey`                 | type   | ForeignKey is a FOREIGN KEY constraint.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `schema.FormatVersion`              | const  | FormatVersion is the version of the schema snapshot JSON format.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `schema.Function`                   | type   | Function is a PostgreSQL function.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `schema.Index`                      | type   | Index is a (possibly unique, partial or expression) index.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `schema.IndexPart`                  | type   | IndexPart is one key of an index.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `schema.KV`                         | type   | KV is an ordered key/value pair.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `schema.Load`                       | func   | Load reads a schema snapshot of any supported format version.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `schema.MariaDBVectorIndexClause`   | func   | MariaDBVectorIndexClause renders a validated index as the clause MariaDB accepts inside CREATE TABLE and ALTER TABLE ...                                                                                          |
| `schema.NormalizeExpr`              | func   | NormalizeExpr returns the canonical spelling of a SQL expression: outside quoted text whitespace is collapsed and letters are lowercased, and redundant enclosing parentheses are removed.                        |
| `schema.NormalizeType`              | func   | NormalizeType returns the canonical spelling of a SQL type so that the declared form and the form reported by a database compare equal.                                                                           |
| `schema.Normalized`                 | func   | Normalized returns a deep copy of s with every type and expression rewritten to its canonical spelling, the Concurrently migration option cleared and the collections sorted.                                     |
| `schema.Partition`                  | type   | Partition describes the partitioning of a parent table.                                                                                                                                                           |
| `schema.PartitionOf`                | type   | PartitionOf describes a child partition.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `schema.Policy`                     | type   | Policy is a row-level security policy.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `schema.RLS`                        | type   | RLS holds a table's row-level security flags (PostgreSQL).                                                                                                                                                        |
| `schema.Schema`                     | type   | Schema is a set of database objects managed by Momo for one dialect.                                                                                                                                              |
| `schema.Schema.Sort`                | method | Sort puts every named collection into a canonical order so that two equivalent schemas serialize identically.                                                                                                     |
| `schema.Schema.Table`               | method | Table returns the table with the given name.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `schema.Schema.Write`               | method | Write encodes the schema as an indented JSON snapshot with a trailing newline, stamping the current FormatVersion.                                                                                                |
| `schema.SchemaNamespace`            | type   | SchemaNamespace is a PostgreSQL schema (namespace) managed by Momo.                                                                                                                                               |
| `schema.Table`                      | type   | Table is a base table.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `schema.Table.Column`               | method | Column returns the column with the given name.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `schema.Table.Index`                | method | Index returns the index with the given name.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `schema.Trigger`                    | type   | Trigger is a table trigger.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `schema.Unique`                     | type   | Unique is a named UNIQUE constraint.                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `schema.ValidateMariaDBVectorIndex` | func   | ValidateMariaDBVectorIndex checks an index whose Method is "vector" against the column.                                                                                                                           |
| `schema.ValidateVectorIndex`        | func   | ValidateVectorIndex checks an index whose Method is "hnsw" or "ivfflat" against the column type, the opclass and the dialect.                                                                                     |

## types

| Identifier                | Kind   | Synopsis                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `types.Codec`             | type   | Codec is the custom-type contract: database/sql scanning, driver value encoding and the SQL type per dialect.                                                                                 |
| `types.Date`              | type   | Date is a calendar date (no time zone): date on PostgreSQL, TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD' on SQLite.                                                                                                      |
| `types.Date.SQLType`      | method | SQLType returns the column type for d.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `types.Date.Scan`         | method | Scan accepts 'YYYY-MM-DD' as string or \[\]byte, or a time.Time (as pgx returns for date columns), whose calendar day in its own location is kept.                                            |
| `types.Date.Value`        | method | Value encodes the date as 'YYYY-MM-DD' using the year, month and day of Time in its own location.                                                                                             |
| `types.Hstore`            | type   | Hstore is map\[string\]*string: hstore on PostgreSQL, TEXT JSON on SQLite.                                                                                                                    |

| `types.Hstore.Scan`       | method | Scan accepts the PostgreSQL hstore text form or a JSON object (string or \[\]byte).                                                                                                           |
| `types.Hstore.Value`      | method | Value returns the hstore text form, e.g.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `types.JSON`              | type   | JSON\[T\] stores any JSON-encodable T: jsonb on PostgreSQL, TEXT on SQLite.                                                                                                                   |
| `types.JSON.SQLType`      | method | SQLType returns the column type for d.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `types.JSON.Scan`         | method | Scan decodes JSON text (string or \[\]byte) into V.                                                                                                                                           |
| `types.JSON.Value`        | method | Value encodes V as JSON text.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `types.ParseUUID`         | func   | ParseUUID parses the canonical 36-character form (dashes at 8, 13, 18, 23) or 32 bare hex digits.                                                                                             |
| `types.TSQuery`           | type   | TSQuery is a PostgreSQL full-text query: tsquery on PostgreSQL, TEXT on SQLite.                                                                                                               |
| `types.TSQuery.SQLType`   | method | SQLType returns the column type for d.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `types.TSQuery.Scan`      | method | Scan accepts the tsquery text form as string or \[\]byte.                                                                                                                                     |
| `types.TSQuery.Value`     | method | Value returns the tsquery text form.                                                                                                                                                          |
| `types.TSVector`          | type   | TSVector is a PostgreSQL full-text document: tsvector on PostgreSQL, TEXT on SQLite (which has no full-text search through Momo).                                                             |
| `types.TSVector.SQLType`  | method | SQLType returns the column type for d.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `types.TSVector.Scan`     | method | Scan accepts the tsvector text form as string or \[\]byte.                                                                                                                                    |
| `types.TSVector.Value`    | method | Value returns the tsvector text form.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `types.TimeOfDay`         | type   | TimeOfDay is a time of day: time on PostgreSQL, TEXT 'HH:MM:SS.uuuuuu' on SQLite.                                                                                                             |
| `types.TimeOfDay.SQLType` | method | SQLType returns the column type for d.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `types.TimeOfDay.Scan`    | method | Scan accepts 'HH:MM:SS' with an optional fraction of 1 to 9 digits (string or \[\]byte).                                                                                                      |
| `types.TimeOfDay.Value`   | method | Value encodes the time as 'HH:MM:SS.uuuuuu', truncated to microseconds because PostgreSQL time has microsecond precision (rounding would turn the last microsecond of the day into 24:00:00). |
| `types.UUID`              | type   | UUID is a 16-byte identifier: uuid on PostgreSQL, TEXT canonical form on SQLite.                                                                                                              |
| `types.UUID.SQLType`      | method | SQLType returns the column type for d.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `types.UUID.Scan`         | method | Scan accepts the canonical 36-character form or 32 bare hex digits (string or \[\]byte), or exactly 16 raw bytes.                                                                             |
| `types.UUID.String`       | method | String returns the canonical 36-character lowercase form.                                                                                                                                     |
| `types.UUID.Value`        | method | Value returns the canonical string, which PostgreSQL casts to uuid.                                                                                                                           |

## vector

Import path: `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/vector`

| Identifier                         | Kind   | Synopsis                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vector.Bits`                      | type   | Bits is a pgvector bit string of Len bits, packed most significant bit first into ceil(Len/8) bytes.                                                                            |
| `vector.Bits.DialectValue`         | method | DialectValue encodes b for dialect d.                                                                                                                                           |
| `vector.Bits.Scan`                 | method | Scan accepts a string of 0 and 1, or a packed \[\]byte blob (sqlite-vec), whose Len becomes 8 times its length.                                                                 |
| `vector.Bits.Validate`             | method | Validate reports whether b is a well-formed bit string of length dim.                                                                                                           |
| `vector.Bits.Value`                | method | Value returns the bit string as a string of 0 and 1.                                                                                                                            |
| `vector.ErrDialect`                | var    | ErrDialect reports a vector type the target dialect cannot store or query.                                                                                                      |
| `vector.ErrInvalidVector`          | var    | ErrInvalidVector reports a vector value that fails validation, such as a dimension mismatch or a non-finite component.                                                          |
| `vector.HalfVector`                | type   | HalfVector is a pgvector halfvec; elements must fit in float16.                                                                                                                 |
| `vector.HalfVector.DialectValue`   | method | DialectValue encodes h for dialect d.                                                                                                                                           |
| `vector.HalfVector.Scan`           | method | Scan accepts pgvector text (string) or a \[\]byte float32 blob.                                                                                                                 |
| `vector.HalfVector.Validate`       | method | Validate is Vector.Validate plus the float16 range.                                                                                                                             |
| `vector.HalfVector.Value`          | method | Value returns the pgvector text form, for example "\[1,2\]".                                                                                                                    |
| `vector.MaxBits`                   | const  | MaxBits is PostgreSQL's limit for the length of a bit string.                                                                                                                   |
| `vector.MaxDim`                    | const  | MaxDim is the storage limit for the dimension of vector and halfvec (pgvector README).                                                                                          |
| `vector.MaxSparseDim`              | const  | MaxSparseDim is the largest sparsevec dimension: pgvector accepts up to 1,000,000,000 dimensions, of which at most MaxSparseNNZ are non-zero.                                   |
| `vector.MaxSparseNNZ`              | const  | MaxSparseNNZ is the largest number of stored elements in a sparsevec.                                                                                                           |
| `vector.SparseVector`              | type   | SparseVector is a pgvector sparsevec.                                                                                                                                           |
| `vector.SparseVector.DialectValue` | method | DialectValue encodes s for dialect d.                                                                                                                                           |
| `vector.SparseVector.Scan`         | method | Scan accepts pgvector sparsevec text ("{2:1,4:2}/5").                                                                                                                           |
| `vector.SparseVector.Validate`     | method | Validate reports whether s has dimension dim and well-formed entries: 1 <= dim <= MaxSparseDim, at most MaxSparseNNZ entries, indices strictly increasing and inside \[0, dim). |
| `vector.SparseVector.Value`        | method | Value returns the pgvector sparsevec text form, "{i:v,...}/dim" with 1-based indices.                                                                                           |
| `vector.Vector`                    | type   | Vector is a pgvector vector (float32 elements).                                                                                                                                 |
| `vector.Vector.DialectValue`       | method | DialectValue encodes v for dialect d.                                                                                                                                           |
| `vector.Vector.Scan`               | method | Scan accepts pgvector text (string) or a sqlite-vec blob (\[\]byte).                                                                                                            |
| `vector.Vector.Validate`           | method | Validate reports whether v has exactly dim finite elements and dim is in 1..MaxDim.                                                                                             |
| `vector.Vector.Value`              | method | Value returns the pgvector text form, for example "\[1,2.5,-3\]".                                                                                                               |

## momotest

Import path: `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/momotest`

| Identifier                   | Kind  | Synopsis                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `momotest.AssertSQL`         | func  | AssertSQL fails the test unless the compiled statement got has the SQL text want, ignoring differences in whitespace.                                                                 |
| `momotest.AssertUsesIndex`   | func  | AssertUsesIndex fails the test unless the query plan of c uses the index named index.                                                                                                 |
| `momotest.DefaultEnv`        | const | DefaultEnv is the environment variable that holds the server URL.                                                                                                                     |
| `momotest.FormatQueryGolden` | func  | FormatQueryGolden renders queries in the golden file format.                                                                                                                          |
| `momotest.Graph`             | func  | Graph returns a step that inserts root with the related rows it includes in one unit, as momo.CreateGraph does: parents first, then root, then children, with foreign keys filled in. |
| `momotest.Insert`            | func  | Insert returns a step that inserts rows one by one, in the order given, reading generated columns (identity keys, defaults) back into each row.                                       |
| `momotest.LoadFixtures`      | func  | LoadFixtures inserts the rows of a YAML file into q, which is a *momo.DB or a *momo.Tx.                                                                                               |
| `momotest.LoadQueryGolden`   | func  | LoadQueryGolden reads a golden file written by QueryGolden, for example the file of the previous release, so a test can run those statements against the current schema.              |
| `momotest.New`               | func  | New returns a *momo.DB on a schema private to t, with the migrations applied.                                                                                                         |
| `momotest.NewTx`             | func  | NewTx returns a *momo.Tx that sees the migrated schema and is rolled back when t finishes, so nothing a test writes outlives it.                                                      |
| `momotest.Option`            | type  | Option configures New and NewTx.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `momotest.ParseQueryGolden`  | func  | ParseQueryGolden parses the golden file format.                                                                                                                                       |
| `momotest.QueryGolden`       | func  | QueryGolden freezes the SQL of a query registry in golden files, one per dialect (dir/postgres.sql, dir/mysql.sql, dir/sqlite.sql; PostgreSQL alone when no dialect is given).        |
| `momotest.RequireEnv`        | const | RequireEnv, set to 1, turns "the server URL is not set" from a skip into a failure.                                                                                                   |
| `momotest.Seed`              | func  | Seed runs the steps in order, so a table that others reference comes first.                                                                                                           |
| `momotest.Step`              | type  | Step is one part of a Seed: it writes fixtures through q.                                                                                                                             |
| `momotest.UpdateGoldenEnv`   | const | UpdateGoldenEnv, set to 1, makes QueryGolden write the golden files instead of comparing against them.                                                                                |
| `momotest.WithEnv`           | func  | WithEnv reads the server URL from the environment variable name instead of MOMO_TEST_POSTGRES_URL.                                                                                    |
| `momotest.WithExtensions`    | func  | WithExtensions creates the named extensions, such as "vector" or "pgcrypto", in the public schema before the migrations run.                                                          |
| `momotest.WithMaxConns`      | func  | WithMaxConns sets the pool size.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `momotest.WithMigrations`    | func  | WithMigrations applies the migrations in fsys, typically an embed.FS narrowed with fs.Sub to the migrations directory, to the database before the test sees it.                       |
| `momotest.WithMomoOptions`   | func  | WithMomoOptions passes opts to momo.New, for example momo.WithHook.                                                                                                                   |

## advisory

Import path: `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/advisory`

| Identifier                   | Kind | Synopsis                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------- | ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `advisory.Hash64`            | func | Hash64 makes a String function hash its key with the 64-bit hashtextextended(key, seed) instead of the 32-bit hashtext.                                              |
| `advisory.Lock`              | func | Lock takes the session-scoped advisory lock for key (pg_advisory_lock) on the pinned connection behind db and waits until it is granted.                             |
| `advisory.LockString`        | func | LockString is Lock with a text key, hashed on the server; see XactLockString for the hash and Hash64 for the 64-bit form.                                            |
| `advisory.Option`            | type | Option changes how the String functions hash their text key.                                                                                                         |
| `advisory.TryLock`           | func | TryLock is the non-blocking form of Lock (pg_try_advisory_lock): it reports whether the lock was granted.                                                            |
| `advisory.TryLockString`     | func | TryLockString is TryLock with a text key, hashed on the server.                                                                                                      |
| `advisory.TryXactLock`       | func | TryXactLock is the non-blocking form of XactLock: it reports whether the lock was granted instead of waiting for it (pg_try_advisory_xact_lock).                     |
| `advisory.TryXactLockString` | func | TryXactLockString is TryXactLock with a hashtext text key.                                                                                                           |
| `advisory.Unlock`            | func | Unlock releases one hold of the session-scoped lock for key (pg_advisory_unlock) and reports whether the session held it.                                            |
| `advisory.UnlockString`      | func | UnlockString is Unlock for a text key.                                                                                                                               |
| `advisory.XactLock`          | func | XactLock takes the transaction-scoped advisory lock for key (pg_advisory_xact_lock) and waits until it is granted.                                                   |
| `advisory.XactLockString`    | func | XactLockString is XactLock with a text key, hashed by the server with hashtext into a 32-bit key (or with hashtextextended into a 64-bit key when Hash64 is passed). |
