| `agg.PercentileDisc`       | func   | PercentileDisc is percentile_disc(fraction) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...): the first input value whose position reaches fraction (0 to 1).                             |
| `agg.String`               | func   | String concatenates the non-NULL values of e, separated by sep, in the order given by OrderBy: string_agg on PostgreSQL, group_concat on SQLite and GROUP_CONCAT ... |
| `agg.ToJSONB`              | func   | ToJSONB converts a value to JSON: to_jsonb(e) on PostgreSQL (a table alias converts the whole row) and json_quote(e) on SQLite.                                      |

## cli

Import path: `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/cli`

| Identifier | Kind | Synopsis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------- | ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cli.Main` | func | Main is the entry point of a custom momo binary: put it in a main function and the binary behaves as momo does (commands, flags, exit codes, diagnostics) with the given generator plugins selectable by name from the plugins section of momo.yaml.                                                                                                                             |
| `cli.Run`  | func | Run executes the momo CLI with args (without the program name), writes its output to stdout and its diagnostics to stderr, and returns the process exit code: 0 for success or current generated code, 1 for stale generated files or generator diagnostics, 2 for a usage, configuration or infrastructure error, and 3 for a database, lock or execution error (momo migrate). |

| `sqlfn.ArithExpr`                   | type   | ArithExpr is a parenthesised binary arithmetic expression over T.                                                                      |

| `sqlfn.ArithExpr.As`                | method | As names the expression in a select list.                                                                                              |
| `sqlfn.Case`                        | func   | Case starts a CASE expression whose branches produce T, for example Case\[string\]().When(host.Excluded().Ne(""), "x").ElseExpr(host). |
| `sqlfn.CaseExpr`                    | type   | CaseExpr is CASE WHEN ...                                                                                                              |
| `sqlfn.CaseExpr.AppendSQL`          | method | AppendSQL writes the CASE expression to b.                                                                                             |
| `sqlfn.CaseExpr.As`                 | method | As names the expression in a select list.                                                                                              |
| `sqlfn.CaseExpr.Else`               | method | Else sets the bound value used when no branch matches.                                                                                 |
| `sqlfn.CaseExpr.ElseExpr`           | method | ElseExpr sets the expression used when no branch matches.                                                                              |
| `sqlfn.CaseExpr.When`               | method | When adds a branch yielding the bound value v.                                                                                         |
| `sqlfn.CaseExpr.WhenExpr`           | method | WhenExpr adds a branch yielding an expression.                                                                                         |
| `sqlfn.Cast`                        | func   | Cast is CAST(e AS sqlType).                                                                                                            |
| `sqlfn.CastExpr`                    | type   | CastExpr is CAST(expr AS type) with a caller-chosen result type T.                                                                     |
| `sqlfn.CastExpr.AppendSQL`          | method | AppendSQL writes the CAST expression to b.                                                                                             |
| `sqlfn.CastExpr.As`                 | method | As names the expression in a select list.                                                                                              |
| `sqlfn.CoalesceExpr`                | func   | CoalesceExpr is COALESCE(a, b, more...): the first non-NULL expression.                                                                |
| `sqlfn.Concat`                      | func   | Concat joins two or more string expressions: (a \|\| b) on PostgreSQL and SQLite, CONCAT(a, b) on MySQL.                               |
| `sqlfn.ConcatExpr`                  | type   | ConcatExpr is string concatenation.                                                                                                    |
| `sqlfn.ConcatExpr.AppendSQL`        | method | AppendSQL writes the concatenation to b.                                                                                               |
| `sqlfn.ConcatExpr.As`               | method | As names the expression in a select list.                                                                                              |
| `sqlfn.CurrentSchema`               | func   | CurrentSchema is current_schema() on PostgreSQL and DATABASE() on MySQL (where a schema is a database).                                |
| `sqlfn.CurrentSchemaExpr`           | type   | CurrentSchemaExpr is the current schema name.                                                                                          |
| `sqlfn.CurrentSchemaExpr.AppendSQL` | method | AppendSQL writes the current_schema call to b.                                                                                         |
| `sqlfn.CurrentSchemaExpr.As`        | method | As names the expression in a select list.                                                                                              |
| `sqlfn.Length`                      | func   | Length is the length of e in characters (CHAR_LENGTH on MySQL, whose LENGTH counts bytes).                                             |
| `sqlfn.LengthExpr`                  | type   | LengthExpr is the character length of a string expression.                                                                             |
| `sqlfn.LengthExpr.AppendSQL`        | method | AppendSQL writes the length call to b.                                                                                                 |
| `sqlfn.LengthExpr.As`               | method | As names the expression in a select list.                                                                                              |
| `sqlfn.Lower`                       | func   | Lower is lower(e).                                                                                                                     |
| `sqlfn.Mul`                         | func   | Mul is e * v.                                                                                                                          |
| `sqlfn.MulExpr`                     | func   | MulExpr is e * other.                                                                                                                  |
| `sqlfn.Numeric`                     | type   | Numeric is the constraint of the arithmetic helpers.                                                                                   |
| `sqlfn.Sub`                         | func   | Sub is e - v.                                                                                                                          |
| `sqlfn.SubExpr`                     | func   | SubExpr is e - other.                                                                                                                  |
| `sqlfn.Substr`                      | func   | Substr is substr(e, from, length): length characters of e starting at the 1-based position from.                                       |
| `sqlfn.SubstrFrom`                  | func   | SubstrFrom is substr(e, from): everything from the 1-based position from.                                                              |
| `sqlfn.Upper`                       | func   | Upper is upper(e).                                                                                                                     |

## timeop

Import path: `github.com/azrtydxb/momo/timeop`

| Identifier                     | Kind   | Synopsis                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------ | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `timeop.AddInterval`           | func   | AddInterval is ts + iv: the timestamp moved forward by the interval.                                                                                                                                    |
| `timeop.AtTimeZone`            | func   | AtTimeZone is (e AT TIME ZONE 'zone') on PostgreSQL: a timestamptz becomes the wall-clock timestamp without time zone in zone, and a timestamp is read as wall-clock in zone and becomes a timestamptz. |
| `timeop.AtTimeZoneExpr`        | func   | AtTimeZoneExpr is AtTimeZone with the zone taken from a string expression, for example a column holding each row's zone.                                                                                |
| `timeop.ClockTimestamp`        | func   | ClockTimestamp is the wall-clock time at the moment it is evaluated: clock_timestamp() on PostgreSQL, which changes within a statement and a transaction, unlike Now.                                   |
| `timeop.CurrentTimestamp`      | func   | CurrentTimestamp is CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, with microsecond precision on MySQL, and the same millisecond text as Now on SQLite.                                                                             |
| `timeop.Expr`                  | type   | Expr is a timestamp-valued expression built by AtTimeZone, AddInterval, SubInterval, Now, CurrentTimestamp or Trunc.                                                                                    |
| `timeop.Expr.AppendSQL`        | method | AppendSQL renders the expression for the dialect of b.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `timeop.Expr.As`               | method | As names the expression in a select list.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `timeop.Extract`               | func   | Extract reads one part of a timestamp: EXTRACT(field FROM e) on PostgreSQL, strftime on SQLite and EXTRACT, DAYOFWEEK and friends on MySQL.                                                             |
| `timeop.ExtractDay`            | const  | The extract fields every dialect can answer.                                                                                                                                                            |

| `timeop.ExtractHour`           | const  | The extract fields every dialect can answer.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `timeop.ExtractISODow`         | const  | The extract fields every dialect can answer.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `timeop.ExtractMinute`         | const  | The extract fields every dialect can answer.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `timeop.ExtractMonth`          | const  | The extract fields every dialect can answer.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `timeop.ExtractQuarter`        | const  | The extract fields every dialect can answer.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `timeop.ExtractSecond`         | const  | The extract fields every dialect can answer.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `timeop.ExtractYear`           | const  | The extract fields every dialect can answer.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `timeop.Interval`              | type   | Interval is a length of time: a count and a unit.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `timeop.IntervalDay`           | const  | The interval units every dialect supports.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `timeop.IntervalExpr`          | func   | IntervalExpr is an interval whose count comes from an integer expression: a column, or momo.Value(n) to bind a parameter.                                                                               |
| `timeop.IntervalHour`          | const  | The interval units every dialect supports.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `timeop.IntervalMinute`        | const  | The interval units every dialect supports.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `timeop.IntervalMonth`         | const  | The interval units every dialect supports.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `timeop.IntervalOf`            | func   | IntervalOf is a literal interval of n units, written into the SQL text (INTERVAL '5 day'), so the same expression in SELECT and GROUP BY stays identical.                                               |
| `timeop.IntervalSecond`        | const  | The interval units every dialect supports.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `timeop.IntervalUnit`          | type   | IntervalUnit is the unit of an Interval.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `timeop.IntervalWeek`          | const  | The interval units every dialect supports.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `timeop.IntervalYear`          | const  | The interval units every dialect supports.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `timeop.Now`                   | func   | Now is the database clock: now() on PostgreSQL (the start of the transaction), NOW(6) on MySQL, and strftime of 'now' in momo's timestamp format on SQLite.                                             |
| `timeop.StatementTimestamp`    | func   | StatementTimestamp is the time the current statement started: statement_timestamp() on PostgreSQL, which differs from Now inside a transaction that runs several statements.                            |
| `timeop.SubInterval`           | func   | SubInterval is ts - iv: the timestamp moved back by the interval.                                                                                                                                       |
| `timeop.Trunc`                 | func   | Trunc rounds a timestamp down to the start of its unit: date_trunc('day', e) on PostgreSQL, and the equivalent strftime or DATE_FORMAT composition on SQLite and MySQL.                                 |
| `timeop.TruncDay`              | const  | The truncation units every dialect supports.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `timeop.TruncHour`             | const  | The truncation units every dialect supports.                                                                                                                                                            |

| `timeop.TruncMonth`            | const  | The truncation units every dialect supports.                                                                                                                                                            |

| `timeop.TruncSecond`           | const  | The truncation units every dialect supports.                                                                                                                                                            |

| `timeop.TruncYear`             | const  | The truncation units every dialect supports.                                                                                                                                                            |

# Source: ARCHITECTURE.md

# Momo architecture

This page describes the packages that exist in the repository and the rules
they follow. It lists no planned packages. For what each database supports see
[capabilities](capabilities.md); for exact signatures read the package
documentation, which is the source of truth.

## Layering

```text
              cmd/momo → cli         cmd/momovet (analyzer binary)
                 │
   ┌─────────────┼──────────────┐
   gen (plugin interface)       migrate ── migrate/{postgres,sqlite,mysql}
   gen/{viz,fromdb,apiquery,    │
        graphql,grpc,openapi}   │
   │                            │
   └──── schema ◄───────────────┘
            ▲
   momo (root runtime) ── dialect, vector, types
            ▲
   driver/{pgxdriver,sqlitedriver,sqlitepure,mysqldriver}
```

Dependency rules. Tests in `internal/repocheck` enforce the first rule and
the two architecture rules below it; the rest are conventions that no test
checks.

1. Enforced by `TestImportGraph` (`go list -deps`): `momo`, `dialect`,
   `schema` and `vector` import only the standard library and each other (the
   root package may also import `types`). No driver, no `golang.org/x/tools`,
   no YAML.
2. Enforced by `TestInternalNeverImportsRoot`: the internal packages the root
   builds on never import the root.
3. Enforced by `TestFeaturePackagesImportOnlyAllowed`: the feature
   subpackages listed in `internal/repocheck/testdata/packages.txt` import only
   the root, the leaf packages and `internal/*`. `TestKnownPackages` forces
   every new package to be given a role in that file.
4. Convention: `driver/*` import `momo` plus their database driver only.
5. Convention: `gen`, `migrate/*`, `cli` and `cmd/*` may import `golang.org/x/tools`,
   YAML and drivers. An application binary that imports only `momo` and one
   driver never links them.
6. Convention: generated code imports only `momo`, `vector`, `types`, `schema`
   and the model package.

## Packages

### `dialect`

`dialect.Dialect` describes one database: its `dialect.Dialect.Name` (`postgres`, `sqlite` or
`mysql`), the MySQL `dialect.Flavor` (`mysql` or `mariadb`), the per-statement bind
limit `MaxParams` and a set of capability flags such as `Returning`,
`OnConflict`, `OnDuplicateKey`, `Locking`, `RowValues`, `Savepoints`,
`ILike` and `Merge`. It also quotes identifiers and writes placeholders.
`dialect.For` returns the dialect for a name and `dialect.MySQLFlavor` the
MySQL or MariaDB variant. The query builder consults these flags and returns
`ErrUnsupported` for what a dialect cannot do.

### `schema`

The neutral description of a database schema: tables, columns, indexes,
foreign keys, checks, enums, views, functions, triggers and policies. It is
what the generator produces from your models, what a migration snapshot
stores, and what each migration dialect inspects from a live database.
`schema.Load` reads a stored schema and refuses a newer `schema.FormatVersion` with
`schema.ErrNewerFormat`. `schema.Equal` and the `Normalize*` functions compare
schemas without being fooled by spelling differences.

### `momo` (root runtime)

- Handles: `DB`, `Tx` and the `Querier` interface that both satisfy.
  `momo.New(driver, opts...)` builds a `DB`.
- The driver contract: `Driver`, `DriverTx` and `Rows`, plus optional
  interfaces a driver can add: `ErrorClassifier`, `Pinner` (a pinned
  connection), `Copier` (bulk copy), `Batcher` (several statements in one
  round trip) and `PoolStater`.
- Typed statements: `Select`, `Insert`, `Update`, `Delete`, `SoftDelete` and
  `Merge`, built from generated column descriptors (`Column[T]`,
  `NullColumn[T]`, `VectorColumn[V]`) and expression builders. Query values
  are immutable: each method returns a modified copy.
- Raw SQL escape hatches: `momo.Exec`, `momo.Scalars`, `momo.Query`, `momo.QueryRows`, `momo.SQL`,
  `momo.TypedSQL` and `RawSubquery`, with `?` positional and `@name` named
  placeholders.
- Relations: generated `Relation` descriptors, `Load`, `LoadAll`, `Preload`
  and the join and write helpers; see [relations](relations.md).
- Transactions, savepoints and pinned connections (`DB.OnConn`).
- Handle options: hooks (`WithHook`), interceptors (`WithInterceptor`, see
  [interceptors](PRIVACY_RULES.md)), read replicas (`WithReplicas`, see
  [replicas](replicas.md)), limits (`WithMaxParams`, `WithMaxInList`) and a
  clock for tests.
- Errors: one `Error` type and the `Err*` sentinels. Match them with
  `errors.Is`, never on message text.

### `vector`

The pgvector value types `vector.Vector`, `vector.HalfVector`, `vector.SparseVector` and `vector.Bits`,
each a `sql.Scanner` and `driver.Valuer` with a `Validate` method, and
`ErrInvalidVector`. A vector field declares its dimension with the tag
`dim:<n>`; the Go type selects the SQL type. See [vectors](vectors.md).

### `types`

Codec types for columns that have no plain Go equivalent: `types.JSON[T]`, `types.Date`,
`types.TimeOfDay`, `types.UUID`, `types.Hstore` and the full-text `types.TSVector` and `types.TSQuery`. See
[type mapping](TYPE_MAPPING.md).

### `driver/*`

| Package               | Database                   | Notes                                           |
| --------------------- | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `driver/pgxdriver`    | PostgreSQL                 | pgx v5 pool or `database/sql`; copy and batch   |
| `driver/sqlitedriver` | SQLite                     | cgo, not on Windows; vectors through sqlite-vec |
| `driver/sqlitepure`   | SQLite                     | pure Go, no vectors                             |
| `driver/mysqldriver`  | MySQL 8.4, 9.7 and MariaDB | vectors: see [capabilities](capabilities.md)    |

### `migrate`

The migration engine: `migrate.Engine` with `migrate.Engine.Diff`, `Plan`, `migrate.Engine.Apply`, `Status`,
`Baseline`, `Drift`, `Resolve`, `Rehash`, `Inspect`, `AutoMigrate`, `Rollback`
and `Rebase`, plus `migrate.ValidateOffline`. A migration directory holds
`<version>_<name>.up.sql`, optional hand-written `.down.sql`, snapshots and
`momo.sum`. A database implements `migrate.Dialect`; the implementations are
`migrate/postgres`, `migrate/sqlite` and `migrate/mysql`, and
`migrate/migratetest` holds helpers for tests. Which of them the `momo migrate`
command runs is generated in [capabilities](capabilities.md); the others are
library APIs. See
[migrations](migrations.md).

### `gen`

The generator. `gen.Load` reads model packages into a `gen.Graph`, `gen.Emit`
writes the generated files through the `Writer`, which is the only file writer
(it refuses targets that are not generated, formats the output and is
deterministic). `gen.Plugin` is the extension interface. Generated Go files
start with `// Code generated by momo (format 1). DO NOT EDIT.`; the header
carries the format number and no release version.

| Package                                 | Purpose                                                       |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `gen/config`                            | `momo.yaml` parsing, shared with the CLI                      |
| `gen/fromdb`                            | models from a PostgreSQL database (`momo generate --from-db`) |
| `gen/viz`                               | Mermaid and DOT diagrams (`momo viz`), also a `gen.Plugin`    |
| `gen/apiquery`                          | cursor, limit and filter helpers for generated APIs           |
| `gen/graphql`                           | GraphQL SDL, gqlgen glue and config, a `gen.Plugin`           |
| `gen/grpc`                              | `.proto`, lock and gRPC servers, a `gen.Plugin`               |
| `gen/openapi`                           | OpenAPI 3.1 document and handlers, a `gen.Plugin`             |
| `gen/naming`, `gen/tags`, `gen/typemap` | naming presets, tag parsing, Go type to SQL type              |

### Other packages

- `cli`: the CLI as a library (`generate`, `migrate`, `viz`, `help`).
  `cli.Main(plugins...)` builds a momo binary with your own generator
  plugins; `cmd/momo` is a thin caller of it with the built-in `graphql`,
  `grpc`, `openapi` and `viz` plugins.
- `momovet` and `cmd/momovet`: the analyzer for non-constant raw SQL; see
  [momovet](momovet.md).
- `momotest`: a schema or a rolled-back transaction per test with your
  migrations applied; `momotest/sqlitetest` is the SQLite variant, kept apart
  so PostgreSQL tests do not link cgo. See [testing](testing.md).
- `momolog`: a `log/slog` hook for statements and relation loads.
- `obs`: ready-made `Hook` and `RelationHook` implementations (a recorder and
  an N+1 relation-load detector); imports only `momo`. See
  [observability](observability.md).
- `importer`, `importer/{gorm,bun,ent}`: static readers of other ORMs' models;
  see [importers](importers.md).
- `bench` is a separate Go module with the comparison benchmarks; see
  [performance](PERFORMANCE.md).

## Test layout

Database tests carry the `integration` build tag, so the default `go test`
run needs no database. `internal/testdb` returns connection strings for a
per-test schema or database, and `internal/testdb/testopen` opens a
`*momo.DB` per dialect, with `testopen.Each` running a test once per dialect
available in the build. CI sets `MOMO_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1`, which turns a
missing database URL from a skip into a failure. Shared feature suites live in
`internal/suite`. See [contributing](contributing.md) for the commands.


# Source: contributing.md

The contributor guide is the `CONTRIBUTING.md` file at the repository root,
included here so the site and the repository stay in sync.

# Contributing to Momo

## Prerequisites

- Go 1.26 or later
- A C toolchain (for the SQLite packages, which use cgo)
- Docker (for `make db-up`, the local integration databases)

## Commands

- `make test`: unit tests, including the separate module `internal/integration` that holds the tests needing gqlgen, gRPC, protoc or the OpenAPI validator
- `make test-race`: unit tests with the race detector
- `make test-compilefail`: compile-fail tests for the typed API
- `make test-integration`: integration tests against real databases

Every test that needs a database lives in a file that starts with the `//go:build integration` tag, next to the SPDX line, and gets its database from `internal/testdb` or `testopen`. `make test`, and the macOS and Windows CI jobs, build without the tag and so run unit tests only; they cannot skip a database test silently because they never compile one. `make test-integration` sets `MOMO_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1`, so an unset database URL fails the run. `TestIntegrationTagConvention` in `internal/repocheck` fails when a file that uses these helpers lacks the tag.

Fuzz targets are listed in `FUZZ_TARGETS` in the Makefile and `make test-fuzz` runs each one for `FUZZTIME`, an execution count. `TestFuzzTargetsListed` fails when a `Fuzz` function is missing from the list.

Dialect coverage is expressed as subtests from `testopen.Each`, one per dialect built into this version; integration tests have no name suffix. `make test-integration-<dialect>` sets that dialect's URL variables and runs the whole suite.

## Documentation pages and Go code blocks

A new page under `docs/` must be added to the `nav` in `mkdocs.yml` and linked from `docs/README.md`; `TestEveryDocPageInNav` and `TestDocsIndexLinksEveryPage` fail otherwise. Every Go block in `docs/` is checked by `TestDocsCodeBlocks`: write a complete `package main` program (it is compiled), or, for a snippet that cannot stand alone, put the comment `<!-- docscheck:fragment -->` on the line before the fence (it must still parse as Go). The number of fragments is capped by `maxFragmentBlocks` in `internal/docscheck/codeblocks_test.go`, so prefer a program. A block marked `<!-- docscheck:run -->` is also executed against PostgreSQL.

An identifier in a backticked span is checked by `TestDocsIdentifiersResolve`: `pkg.Name` must exist. A bare name such as `Select` means the root `momo` package. When only a feature package exports it (`Case` is in `sqlfn`), `TestBareNamesAreRootNames` fails with the file, the line and the suggestion `sqlfn.Case`; write the qualified name; the same holds for a method such as `migrate.Engine.Apply`. A collision in prose is fixed by qualifying, never by removing the backticks. A page whose section names the package may keep bare names if `internal/docscheck/testdata/bare_allow.txt` lists the page and the package with a reason.

## Exported API changes need a docs change

The `apidiff-docs` CI job (`make apidiff-gate`, `scripts/apidiff-docs-gate.sh`) runs `golang.org/x/exp/cmd/apidiff`, pinned in the Makefile, between the base branch and your branch for the root package and every non-internal subpackage. Any exported change, compatible or incompatible, fails the job unless one of two things holds:

- the diff touches `README.md`, `llms.txt`, a Markdown page under `docs/` (`docs/**/*.md`) or an `examples/**/README.md` (other files under `docs/` and `examples/` do not count); or
- the pull request body, or a commit message in the range, has a line that starts in column 0 with `Docs: no reader-visible change: ` followed by a real reason, for example `Docs: no reader-visible change: internal helper exposed for tests`. A blank reason, a `<placeholder>` such as `<reason>`, and an indented or quoted line are rejected.

A change to a Go comment or an unexported identifier produces an empty report and needs neither. The job lives in its own workflow, `.github/workflows/apidiff-docs.yml`, so it also runs when the PR body is edited: add the escape line to the body and the check re-evaluates without a new commit. The job reads the live body, not the stale event payload. It keeps one comment (marked `<!-- apidiff-docs -->`) with the apidiff report, and posts none when the API did not change. Run it locally with `make apidiff-gate`.

## Root package file names

Every non-test `.go` file in the repository root is `doc.go` or is named with one of the prefixes `db`, `tx`, `driver`, `err`, `build`, `meta`, `expr`, `col`, `select`, `insert`, `update`, `delete`, `upsert`, `write`, `raw` or `rel`, either bare (`db.go`) or followed by an underscore and a topic (`expr_ops.go`). A test file is named after its subject file where it has one (`foo_test.go`, `foo_internal_test.go` or `foo_integration_test.go` for a subject `foo.go`; a longer topic such as `foo_bar_integration_test.go` is fine). The guard checks only the prefix: a test file's name without `_test` must itself start with one of the prefixes, and a test that spans several files takes the prefix of the area it tests. `TestRootFilePrefixes` in `internal/repocheck` fails on any other name and lists the prefixes in its message. There is no exception list: rename the file instead.

## Commit messages and PR titles

Commit messages and PR titles use Conventional Commits: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`,
`refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`. Mark breaking
changes with `feat!:` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.

## SPDX headers

Every new `.go` file starts with this header, followed by a blank line before
`package`:

```go
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

package example
```

Generated files begin with `// Code generated by momo` instead.
